papers.abstract_en: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by marked spatial immune heterogeneity, commonly manifested as immune‑desert, immune‑excluded and immune‑inflamed phenotypes. These phenotypes are closely associated with variable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Emerging evidence suggests that they are shaped not only by canonical immune pathways but also by mitochondrial processes that regulate immune priming, T‑cell trafficking and the maintenance of effector function. The present review summarizes how mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial DNA‑cGAS‑STING signaling, pathways mediated by tricarboxylic acid cycle metabolites, and non‑cell‑autonomous mitochondrial transfer may contribute to the establishment and maintenance of distinct spatial immune phenotypes in NSCLC. It is proposed that insufficient activation of innate immunity and impaired dendritic cell priming are particularly relevant to immune‑desert tumors, whereas chronic oxidative stress may reinforce barriers mediated by cancer‑associated fibroblasts (CAFs), transforming growth factor β, and the extracellular matrix in immune‑excluded tumors. By contrast, immune‑inflamed tumors may represent a state in which pre‑existing immune circuitry remains intact and tumor‑infiltrating lymphocytes retain greater mitochondrial fitness and metabolic resilience. The implications of these mechanisms for ICI sensitivity and cold‑to‑hot tumor conversion strategies were further discussed. Current evidence from human studies remains largely correlative, and prospective, spatially resolved functional studies are needed. Nevertheless, integrating mitochondrial biology with spatial immune architecture within a phenotype‑guided framework may generate testable hypotheses for future biomarker development and combination strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Objective.To develop a conditional vector-quantized (VQ) diffusion-based dynamic cone beam computed tomography imaging framework using dual-view x-ray projections for accurate reconstruction of respiratory-induced lung tumor motion, with the potential to enable four-dimensional (4D) target verification during lung radiotherapy.Methods.Patient-specific respiratory motion models were constructed from planning 4D- computed tomography(CT) images using deformable image registration and principal component analysis (PCA). Synthetic DVFs were generated by sampling PCA coefficients and applied to the reference-phase CT images to produce dynamic three-dimensional (3D) volumes, from which paired dual-view DRRs were generated. A conditional VQ diffusion framework was developed, consisting of separate two-dimensional and 3D vector quantized variational autoencoder s for encoding DRRs and DVFs into discrete latent representations, followed by a conditional diffusion model to learn the mapping from x-ray projection features to deformation vector field (DVF) latent representations. During inference, dual-view x-ray projections were encoded and processed by the conditional diffusion model to estimate DVFs, which were then used to deform the reference CT image and reconstruct temporally resolved 3D volumes.Results.The simulation study demonstrates that the estimated DVFs effectively captured the respiratory-induced deformation of lung tumors, and the reconstructed dynamic volume CT images demonstrated accurate anatomical motion characteristics across respiratory phases.Conclusion.The proposed patient-specific VQ diffusion framework enables accurate estimation of respiratory-induced lung tumor motion from dual-view x-ray projections and facilitates the high-temporal-resolution dynamic volume CT reconstruction. The results demonstrate its potential as an image-guided solution for tumor motion tracking in lung tumor radiotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are critical drivers of tumor progression and therapeutic resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, how CSCs remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) of NSCLC remains largely unclear. METHODS: Flow cytometry was performed to evaluate the immunomodulatory effects of NSCLC CSCs on T cell differentiation. RNA-sequencing-based metabolic profiling was conducted to identify pivotal metabolic pathways activated in CSCs. Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) encapsulated in CSC-derived exosomes were quantified, and the molecular mechanism by which exosomal ROS modulates intracellular nitric oxide (NO) production and FoxP3 post-translational modifications in T cells was further explored. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) were utilized as a preclinical model to verify the therapeutic potential of glutamine metabolism targeting. RESULTS: NSCLC CSCs potently induced tumor immunosuppression by promoting regulatory T (Treg) cell differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperactive glutamine metabolism in CSCs substantially increased mitochondrial ROS generation. Exosomal ROS secreted by CSCs was transferred to T cells, thereby elevating intracellular NO synthesis. Increased NO further triggered S-nitrosylation and deubiquitination of FoxP3, which ultimately stabilized FoxP3 expression and facilitated Treg cell differentiation. In NSCLC PDO models, pharmacological inhibition of glutamine metabolism reversed the immunosuppressive T cell phenotype and efficiently suppressed PDO growth. CONCLUSION: NSCLC CSCs mediate TME immunosuppression via a glutamine metabolism-dependent regulatory axis. Exosomal ROS-initiated FoxP3 post-translational modification is a novel mechanism underlying CSC-driven Treg differentiation. This study reveals an unreported immune evasion pathway in NSCLC and identifies glutamine metabolism as a viable therapeutic target for overcoming tumor immunosuppression.

papers.abstract_en: Uncommon epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma comprises clinically and biologically heterogeneous subgroups with variable sensitivity to targeted therapy. Incomplete responses and eventual progression suggest that factors beyond receptor inhibition influence disease persistence during therapy. This hypothesis-generating narrative review examines whether apoptosis repressor with caspase recruitment domain (ARC), encoded by nucleolar protein 3 (NOL3), warrants investigation as a downstream node in the regulation of apoptosis within an aging-informed framework. The available evidence is considered across three levels: direct evidence from uncommon EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma; evidence from broader EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma or lung cancer; and evidence extrapolated from other cancers or nonmalignant tissues. Within the literature evaluated, no primary study directly demonstrated mutation-specific ARC/NOL3 enrichment, induction after EGFR inhibition, functional dependence, or an association with post-treatment tumor cell survival or clinical outcomes in uncommon EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. Accordingly, established ARC functions in caspase regulation, mitochondrial protection, and stress tolerance are not interpreted as evidence of disease-specific causality. Instead, they provide a biological rationale for testing whether uncommon EGFR signaling, regulation of apoptosis, and aging-associated stress responses intersect in selected tumor contexts. We outline the experimental and clinical evidence required to evaluate this hypothesis, including mutation-specific expression analyses, functional perturbation studies, longitudinal sampling, and biomarker validation. The framework identifies experimental and clinical priorities for evaluating the potential role of ARC/NOL3 in this disease setting.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) represents the most prevalent type of lung cancer, accounting for 35‑40% of all lung cancer cases. Regulatory T cells (Tregs), a CD4+ T cell subtype with immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal role in maintaining self‑tolerance under physiological conditions. Recent evidence has increasingly highlighted their involvement in various cancers. In LUAD, Treg infiltration into tissues undermines the immune anticancer response, correlating with disease stage, treatment efficacy and prognosis. By inhibiting robust anti‑tumor immune mechanisms, Tregs facilitate tumor immune escape in LUAD. Furthermore, elevated Treg cell accumulation in LUAD has been linked to reduced overall survival rates. Tregs serve as independent predictors for LUAD diagnosis in patients at high risk of recurrence. Systematic depletion of all Tregs to enhance anticancer efficacy poses risks of inducing severe autoimmune pathologies. Consequently, understanding the precise structure of tumor‑infiltrating Tregs is essential for effective targeting of these cells in tumors. Additionally, identifying candidate targets or methods for the specific elimination of tumor‑infiltrating Tregs is necessary for developing efficient and safe combination immunotherapy strategies for LUAD. The present study focuses on the regulatory role of Tregs in LUAD prognosis, immune escape and targeted therapies, elucidating the molecular mechanisms of Treg involvement and presenting associated therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. As a predominant immune cell population in the tumor microenvironment (TME), tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) play a critical role in tumor progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). TAMs can promote either antitumor immunity or immunosuppression depending on their polarization status. Iron regulatory protein 2 (IRP2) is a key regulator of intracellular iron homeostasis and has been reported to be upregulated in several tumor types. However, the role of IRP2 in the TME remains unclear. This study revealed the previously unrecognized role of IRP2 in NSCLC progression and explored its potential as a TAM-directed therapeutic target linked to programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) regulation. We found that IRP2 skewed TAMs toward an immunosuppressive state that promoted tumor cell proliferation and migration, and limited apoptosis. Furthermore, IRP2 may sustain PD-L1 expression in TAMs by limiting sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1)-associated lysosomal degradation. In conclusion, our findings identify IRP2-dependent maintenance of the immunosuppressive TAM phenotype as a promising therapeutic target in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Lung and ovarian cancers account for substantial cancer morbidity and mortality worldwide. Plant-derived natural products represent promising alternatives in cancer therapy because of their structural diversity and ability to target multiple signaling pathways. Prosopis species are ethnomedicinal plants traditionally known for their antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities; however, their anticancer potential remains poorly explored. This study evaluates the anticancer properties of extracts of Prosopis cineraria, Prosopis farcta, and Prosopis juliflora, the Prosopis species growing in Qatar, against human lung (A549) and ovarian (SK-OV-3) cancer cells. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used to characterize their phytochemical composition. The cytotoxicity and anti-migratory activity of the three extracts were evaluated. Western blot analysis was performed to investigate the molecular effects of the extracts on proliferation- and apoptosis-related proteins. GC-MS profiling identified diverse low-molecular-weight bioactive compounds across the extracts, including several compounds detected only in P. juliflora, which exhibited the most potent cytotoxicity toward A549 and SK-OV-3 cells. All three extracts inhibited cancer cell migration, with P. juliflora showing the strongest effect. Furthermore, P. juliflora reduced the expression of proliferation and survival markers and increased the expression of pro-apoptotic proteins. These findings identify P. juliflora as the most active of the three tested Prosopis extracts and support further investigation of its in vitro anticancer potential.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Routine assessment of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and comprehensive next-generation sequencing (NGS) is recommended to guide treatment selection in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Obtaining adequate tissue for biomarker and molecular analyses is therefore essential. This study compared sample adequacy for PD-L1 and NGS testing between shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) and computed tomography-guided transthoracic lung biopsy (CTTB) in patients with NSCLC. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with NSCLC who underwent biopsy of PPL by ssRAB or CTTB between June 2020 and December 2025. Demographic, procedural, pathological, biomarker and molecular data were extracted from electronic medical records, and descriptive statistics analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed. RESULTS: A total of 402 patients were included, comprising 198 in the ssRAB cohort and 204 in the CTTB cohort. ssRAB demonstrated significantly higher sample adequacy rates than CTTB for both PD-L1 (98.8% vs. 90.6%, p < 0.001) and NGS testing (92.3% vs. 79.1%, p = 0.005). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, ssRAB was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 sample adequacy (adjusted OR 11.48, 95% CI 2.89-78.30; p = 0.002) and NGS sample adequacy (adjusted OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.64-11.40; p = 0.004) compared with CTTB. In a separate model evaluating biopsy tools, cryobiopsy use was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 adequacy (adjusted OR 16.54, 95% CI 2.92-317.65; p = 0.010) and NGS adequacy (adjusted OR 5.83, 95% CI 1.93-25.39; p = 0.006) compared with non-cryobiopsy sampling. CONCLUSIONS: ssRAB-acquired specimens were associated with higher rates of PD-L1 and NGS sample adequacy than CTTB-acquired specimens in patients with NSCLC. Future prospective studies are needed to better understand the procedural and specimen-related factors underlying these differences.

papers.abstract_en: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially fatal immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung cancer, and many machine-learning (ML), computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models have been proposed to predict it. This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and SinoMed, supplemented by citation searching and other sources, with independent dual-reviewer screening throughout and a reproducible PubMed verification search updated to August 16, 2026. Twelve peer-reviewed lung-cancer CIP-occurrence models (4,875 patients, 1,057 events) formed the main analysis; validation C-statistics were pooled on the logit scale with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp intervals, stratified by validation design. The pooled validation C-statistic was 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.75-0.88) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 90.7%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.51-0.95, which is the decision-relevant quantity. By validation design, internal cross-validation pooled to 0.83, internal split-sample to 0.76, and only two studies reported external validation (0.84 and 0.92, described narratively). Imaging-based models (k = 8) showed numerically higher discrimination than clinical models (k = 4; 0.85 versus 0.78, moderator p = 0.46) without a statistically significant difference, and this comparison is confounded by design covariates. Estimates were stable on leave-one-out, alternative-model, cohort-overlap, and standard-error-source sensitivity analyses (range 0.80-0.84). Under the standard Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, applied independently by two reviewers with consensus resolution, two studies were at high, nine at unclear, and one at low overall risk of bias; certainty of evidence was low (very low under a stricter appraisal scenario, which left the pooled estimate essentially unchanged). Current models separate risk groups on average but remain unready for clinical use; adequately powered, externally validated, and calibration-reported models are needed.

papers.abstract_en: To evaluate the clinical utility of combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation analysis in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) for lung cancer diagnosis using methylation-specific PCR (MSP). The study aimed to combine BALF methylation results with bronchoscopic cytology, serum tumor markers, and imaging data to assess their diagnostic value. A total of 77 patients were recruited and divided into two groups: 57 patients with lung cancer and 20 control subjects. The methylation levels of SHOX2 and RASSF1A in BALF samples were analyzed using MSP. General data, serum markers, imaging, cytology, and pathology results were collected. The methylation levels were compared between the two groups, and differences in methylation levels across different pathological types and stages were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to determine the cutoff values. The diagnostic performance of combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation testing was compared with serum markers and cytology. The combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation test showed a sensitivity of 68.42% and a specificity of 95%, significantly improving the detection rate of lung adenocarcinoma. Higher methylation levels were observed in advanced-stage lung cancer compared with early-stage cases. The combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation test exhibited the highest sensitivity, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.817, compared with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), cytokeratin 19 fragment 21-1 (CY211), and BALF cytology. The combined use of BALF cytology and methylation testing increased the detection rate to 73.68%, higher than BALF cytology alone (40.35%). The odds ratio for positive SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation in patients with bronchial cutoff signs was 15.167. Combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation testing can serve as an auxiliary diagnostic tool for lung cancer, outperforming serum markers and BALF cytology in diagnostic efficacy. Additionally, it can complement BALF cytology and provide a more accurate diagnosis. The presence of bronchial cutoff signs can be used as a relevant factor to predict positive SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation.

papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to investigate the interventional effects of Kaixin Powder(KXP) on the progression of lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD) under chronic stress and its underlying mechanism. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry(UPLC-MS/MS) was employed to characterize the chemical constituents of KXP, followed by network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses to screen for its potential targets. A chronic stress-associated lung cancer mouse model was established by axillary inoculation of Lewis lung carcinoma(LLC) cells combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress(CUMS). Sixty SPF-grade C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into the following groups: normal group, lung cancer group, model group, low-and high-dose KXP(13.65 and 27.3 g·kg~(-1)) groups, and fluoxetine(2 mg·kg~(-1)) group. Tumor growth indicators, including body weight, tumor mass, and tumor inhibition rate of mice were measured. Depression-like behaviors were observed by open field test(OFT) and sucrose preference test(SPT). Serum levels of stress factors such as corticosterone(Cort) and kynurenine(Kyn) were measured by ELISA. Histopathological changes in tumor tissue were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin(HE) staining. Peripheral blood T lymphocyte subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry. Intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration was detected by immunofluorescence, and the protein expression levels of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1(IDO1) and aryl hydrocarbon receptor(Ahr) were determined by Western blot. Serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels were measured to evaluate hepatic and renal safety. UPLC-MS/MS analysis characterized 157 chemical constituents of KXP. The protein expression levels of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1(IDO1) and aryl hydrocarbon receptor(Ahr) were detected by Western blot. In addition, serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels were measured to evaluate hepatic and renal safety. UPLC-MS identified 157 chemical constituents of KXP. Network pharmacology analysis obtained 367 potential targets, among which epidermal growth factor receptor(EGFR), protein kinase B alpha(AKT1), signal transducer and activator of transcription 3(STAT3), heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1(HSP90AA1), and IDO1 were screened as core targets. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes(KEGG) pathway analysis and molecular docking indicated that abnormal tryptophan metabolism mediated by IDO1 may be a potential mechanism underlying KXP intervention in LUAD complicated with depression. Animal experiments showed that, compared with the lung cancer group, the model group exhibited significantly accelerated tumor growth, increased structural disarray and atypia in HE-stained tumor tissue, obvious depression-like behaviors, and significantly elevated serum Cort and Kyn levels. In addition, the proportions of peripheral blood CD3~+ and CD3~+CD4~+T cells and the CD3~+CD4~+/CD3~+CD8~+ ratio significantly decreased, whereas the proportion of CD3~+CD8~+T cells significantly increased. Intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration was reduced, while the protein expression levels of IDO1 and Ahr were significantly upregulated. Compared with the model group, the high-dose KXP group showed significantly reduced tumor volume and tumor weight, with a tumor inhibition rate of 52.43%. KXP intervention improved depression-like behaviors to varying degrees, with the high-dose group showing more pronounced improvements in OFT activity indicators and SPT sucrose preference rate. Serum Cort and Kyn levels were significantly reduced in the high-dose KXP group. The proportions of peripheral blood CD3~+ and CD3~+CD4~+T cells and the CD3~+CD4~+/CD3~+CD8~+ ratio significantly increased in both low-and high-dose KXP groups. The low-dose KXP group showed significantly reduced IDO1 protein expression, while the high-dose group showed significantly reduced expression of both IDO1 and Ahr proteins. Safety evaluation showed that, within the experimental dose range, KXP had no obvious adverse effects on the morphology of major organs or on serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels. In conclusion, KXP ameliorates chronic stress and delays LUAD progression, and its mechanism may be associated with inhibition of the IDO1/Kyn/Ahr axis, correction of abnormal tryptophan metabolism, promotion of intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration, and improvement of the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: Radon is a globally recognized lung carcinogen and one of the main risk factors for lung cancer in nonsmokers. In Peru, recent evidence indicates elevated radon concentrations in homes in Metropolitan Lima and a possible contribution to the increase in lung cancer, especially in women, although national evidence primarily comes from ecological studies and is still insufficient to establish causality. Regulatory, technical, and surveillance gaps persist that hinder its control. This special article presents a narrative review of international and national evidence and aims to examine the current situation of radon exposure in Peru, identify the regulatory and surveillance gaps that limit its control, and propose specific mitigation measures aligned with international recommendations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is one of the most common cancers in Germany and is predominantly detected at an advanced stage. To ensure early detection, the German Social Accident Insurance (DGUV) offers lung cancer screening including a low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) for individuals with long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust and a smoking history of at least 30 pack years. Younger individuals (OR: 0.96, p < 0.001), individuals with prolonged exposure to asbestos dust (OR: 1.01, p = 0.011) and with a history of pneumonia (OR: 1.16, p = 0.011) were more likely to undergo LDCT screening. papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for accurate, automated, and clinically interpretable diagnostic systems. Although existing deep learning (DL) models have achieved promising performance in classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant, most approaches are limited to binary classification and provide insufficient support for detailed tumor characterization and TNM staging. Furthermore, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective in extracting local morphological features but often fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies. In contrast, transformer-based models can learn global contextual information but may compromise fine-grained local feature representation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with Radiomic Feature Fusion (ReViT-RF) framework for lung tumor classification and component-wise TNM stage prediction using thoracic computed tomography (CT) images from the publicly available Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. The primary clinical objectives of the proposed framework are to: (i) classify pulmonary nodules as benign or malignant, and (ii) predict individual TNM components, including primary tumor extent (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastatic status (M) for malignant cases. To improve tumor visibility and image quality, CT images are initially preprocessed using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and intensity normalization. The proposed ReViT-RF architecture integrates the complementary advantages of ResNet-50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) for comprehensive feature learning. The CNN branch extracts local morphological, textural, and structural characteristics, whereas the transformer branch captures long-range spatial relationships and global contextual dependencies. In addition, handcrafted radiomic features, including shape, size, texture, and spatial descriptors, are fused with deep features to provide clinically meaningful information for accurate TNM component prediction. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio, with data augmentation applied only to the training set to prevent information leakage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 97.62% for benign-malignant classification, along with high precision, recall, and F1-score values. Moreover, independent prediction of TNM components provides detailed stage-related information rather than relying on a single aggregated stage label, enabling more precise tumor assessment and clinical decision support. Furthermore, explainability analysis using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) identifies the critical tumor regions contributing to model predictions, improving interpretability and enhancing clinician confidence. Overall, by combining hybrid deep feature extraction, radiomic feature fusion, component-wise TNM stage prediction, and explainable AI analysis, the proposed ReViT-RF framework provides a reliable, comprehensive, and clinically interpretable solution for automated lung tumor analysis.

EX(+ )/STAS(-) and EX(+ )/STAS(+) groups showed significantly shorter RFS than EX(-)/STAS(-) group, but EX(-)/STAS(+) group did not. In conclusion, EX was associated with poor prognosis after sublobar resection of lung adenocarcinoma. Combined evaluation of EX and STAS may improve postoperative risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma is the most prevalent subtype of non-small cell lung cancer and exhibits a high tendency for distant metastasis. However, uterine metastasis with synchronous multiorgan involvement is extremely rare and prone to misdiagnosis due to atypical clinical presentations. To date, fewer than 20 cases of lung adenocarcinoma metastasizing to the uterus have been documented globally, most of which present with typical gynecological symptoms, making our atypical case highly educational and complementary to existing clinical data. CASE: Herein, we describe a 77-year-old postmenopausal female patient who initially presented with lumbago and dizziness without typical pulmonary or gynecological symptoms, with an ECOG performance status of 1. Imaging studies raised suspicion of a primary uterine malignancy, but pathological biopsy, immunohistochemistry, and genomic testing ultimately confirmed advanced lung adenocarcinoma with multiorgan metastases (uterus, lung, liver, bone). Molecular analysis identified an EGFR exon 21 p.L858R mutation, and the patient received palliative local radiotherapy combined with osimertinib targeted therapy. During treatment, the patient developed mild radiation-induced fatigue and slight myelosuppression, which were fully relieved after symptomatic supportive care, with no severe unexpected adverse events observed. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates the atypical metastatic pattern of lung adenocarcinoma, underscores the pivotal role of pathological and immunohistochemical examinations in differentiating primary from metastatic tumors, and offers a reference for managing diagnostically challenging cases. Early and accurate diagnosis coupled with genomic-guided personalized therapy is critical for enhancing quality of life and prognosis in patients with advanced lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: In recent years, pulmonary segmentectomy has become a preferred treatment option for early-stage lung cancer. The primary factor encouraging clinicians to choose segmentectomy is the assumption of greater parenchymal preservation. METHODS: Preoperative and postoperative thoracic computed tomography scans of patients diagnosed with lung cancer between January 2022 and December 2025 who underwent robotic lobectomy or segmentectomy were analyzed using Synapse 3D software. Differences between predicted and measured values were analyzed using the independent-samples t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, depending on the data distribution. RESULTS: A total of 39 patients were included in the study. Lobectomy was performed in 21 patients, and segmentectomy in 18. The median resected lung volume was 360.5 mL (interquartile range [IQR]: 198-550) in the segmentectomy group and 896 mL (IQR: 599-1194) in the lobectomy group (P < .001). The difference in expected remaining lung volume percentages between the lobectomy and segmentectomy groups was statistically significant (P < .001), whereas the difference in measured postoperative remaining lung volumes was not statistically significant (P = .1). CONCLUSION: This pilot study demonstrated that robotic segmentectomy may not provide the expected parenchymal preservation advantage compared with lobectomy. Further prospective multicenter studies with larger cohorts are required.

GSTM1 expression was higher in tumour tissue in the combined NSCLC group and in the SCC subgroup and was also higher in SCC than in AC tumours (p<0.05). GSTT1 expression was higher in AC than SCC tumours (p<0.05). CYP1B1 and GSTP1 were highly expressed in both tissue compartments but showed no significant tumour-specific increase. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cigarette smoke contains numerous toxic compounds that can induce oxidative stress and DNA damage. While smoking is a well-established driver of lung cancer initiation, the biological consequences of continued exposure after tumor establishment remain poorly understood. This study investigated the genomic and phenotypic effects of chronic cigarette smoke exposure in established lung cancer cells. METHODS: Human lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells were chronically exposed to cigarette smoke extract to model sustained exposure. Cellular proliferation and migration assays were performed to evaluate phenotypic changes. Transcriptomic profiling was used to examine alterations in gene expression related to cell cycle regulation and DNA repair pathways. Whole-genome sequencing was conducted to identify mutational signatures associated with genomic instability. Tumor growth and histological features were further evaluated using xenograft models. RESULTS: Chronic cigarette smoke extract exposure increased the clonogenic capacity and migratory behavior of A549 cells and induced phenotypic features consistent with partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Transcriptomic analysis revealed disruption of cell cycle regulation and reduced expression of homologous recombination DNA repair genes, including RAD51. Whole-genome sequencing identified mutational signatures associated with oxidative damage, mismatch repair deficiency, and homologous recombination defects. These alterations were accompanied by increased tumor growth and cellular atypia in xenograft models. CONCLUSIONS: Chronic cigarette smoke exposure may enhance genomic instability and promote aggressive phenotypes in established lung cancer cells, suggesting that continued smoking after cancer development may contribute to tumor progression.

papers.abstract_en: Mediastinal nodal classification in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) at the N0/N1-N2/N3 treatment-defining boundary guides therapeutic strategy and is commonly finalized in multidisciplinary tumor board (MDT) meetings. Relative to the MDT category, PET/CT over-classified 16 patients (14.0%) and under-classified 9 (7.9%). EBUS-TBNA under-classified 15 of the 43 patients it classified N0/N1 (34.9%), and under-classification persisted among the 25 patients in whom every sampled station was diagnostic (8/25, 32.0%); 12 of these 15 assignments rested on clinical-radiological course rather than histopathology. Agreement with the MDT category was 85.1% (κ = 0.662) for EBUS-TBNA and 78.1% (κ = 0.389) for PET/CT; because malignant cytology was definitional for the MDT category, 67 of 97 concordant EBUS-TBNA classifications (69.1%) were determined by that rule and do not measure EBUS-TBNA performance. These findings are consistent with guideline recommendations that PET-positive mediastinal nodes require tissue confirmation and that a negative endosonographic result be interpreted alongside pretest probability and station coverage.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary papillary adenoma is currently considered a benign tumor; however, a few cases have been reported in the past with potential for malignancy. Therefore, the histological nature of papillary adenomas remains controversial. This article presents a rare case of a multifocal papillary adenoma with uncertain malignant potential, featuring an ERBIN-BRAF gene fusion and an APC mutation, along with a literature review, to enhance understanding of this tumor. CASE DESCRIPTION: The patient sought medical consultation due to symptoms of cough and sputum production. Imaging showed a high-density, lobulated nodule in the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe, surrounded by multiple smaller nodules. Postpulmonary lobectomy, histopathological examination revealed a large nodule composed of a single papillary structure, with the papillary surface covered by a single layer of cuboidal or low-columnar epithelium. Local areas showed transition to surrounding alveolar epithelium, and well-formed glands were observed in the proliferative fibrous tissue, with local stromal fibrosis. Some tumor cells in the surrounding small nodules grew in a lepidic fashion, with cellular morphology similar to that of the large nodule. Immunohistochemical staining showed that tumor cells were positive for TTF-1, CK, CK7, and Napsin A, with a few cells expressing P53 and a Ki-67 index of approximately 8%. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified an APC gene mutation (Exon 16, p.E1306∗) and an ERBIN exon3-BRAF exon11 fusion. Given that BRAF alterations have been implicated in lung carcinogenesis, a similar BRAF-mediated tumorigenic pathway may be active in this tumor; therefore, complete resection of the adenoma may be indicated. The tumor's multifocal distribution and molecular alterations suggest that this case represents a papillary adenoma with uncertain malignant potential. CONCLUSIONS: Currently, there is no established standard treatment for such tumors, and the tumor in this case underwent pulmonary lobectomy. Future studies should accumulate more cases to clarify the prognosis and treatment guidelines for this type of tumor.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Several therapeutic targets for non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) rely on protein expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Most biomarkers are validated on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue; however, cytologic specimens, including cell blocks (CBs), that are subject to preanalytical variables are increasingly used. The objective of this study was to evaluate predictive IHC biomarkers in NSCLC CBs and compare them with surgical pathology (SP) specimens. METHODS: The authors retrospectively reviewed NSCLC cytology specimens that underwent predictive IHC testing for hepatocyte growth factor receptor (c-MET), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), and programmed death-ligand-1 (PD-L1) between January 2019 and June 2025. IHC was performed on CBs that were centrifuged with equal amounts of ethanol and formalin before FFPE processing. Equal numbers of NSCLC SP specimens with available biomarker testing were included for comparison. Predictive IHC scores that were considered therapy-eligible were c-MET IHC 3+, HER2 IHC 3+, and PD-L1-positive tumor proportion scores. Statistical analyses were performed using the Fisher exact test, with p < .05 considered significant. RESULTS: The cohort included 414 cases (cytology specimens, N = 212; SP specimens, N = 212 [60% biopsy, 40% resection]). Cytology specimens demonstrated a significantly higher proportion of strong 3+ c-MET expression (40%) compared with SP specimens (10%; p < .0001). Similarly, high PD-L1 expression was more frequent in cytology specimens (32% vs. 20%; p = .0079). HER2 expression was similar between groups, with no significant difference in HER2 IHC 3+ rates (p = .34). CONCLUSIONS: Predictive IHC testing is performed on NSCLC cytology to identify patients for therapeutic targets. The current study highlights the need for optimizing preanalytical variables in cytology specimen processing, even when testing FFPE CBs, to ensure the reliability of predictive IHC results that guide therapeutic decisions.

papers.abstract_en: Acquired resistance to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeted therapy remains a major obstacle in the treatment of EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study investigated whether repurposing mebendazole (MBZ), a microtubule-disrupting agent, could restore sensitivity to gefitinib in gefitinib-resistant HCC827 GR5 cells. Gefitinib monotherapy showed minimal cytotoxicity, reducing cell viability only marginally (92.7 ± 1.5%), whereas MBZ significantly decreased viability to 79.7 ± 0.6% at 0.1 µM and 29.7 ± 0.6% at 0.5 µM (p < 0.001). Combination treatment (gefitinib 1 µM + MBZ 0.1 µM) further reduced viability to 37.7 ± 0.6% (p < 0.001). Mechanistically, alkaline comet assay revealed significantly increased single-strand DNA damage in the combination group (tail intensity 22.33 ± 0.56%, p < 0.001), while neutral comet assay confirmed elevated double-strand DNA breaks. MBZ also induced dose-dependent γ-H2AX activation (p < 0.001), supporting replication stress-associated DNA damage signaling. In vivo, combination therapy significantly suppressed tumor growth, prolonging tumor doubling time from 6.2 days in controls to 25 days and increasing growth delay to 18.8 days (p < 0.01), without substantial systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings identify replication stress vulnerability as a therapeutically exploitable axis and support MBZ repurposing as an adjuvant strategy to overcome gefitinib resistance.

papers.abstract_en: In real-world clinical settings, patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) display significant heterogeneity, highlighting the need to identify key prognostic biomarkers and clinical factors. This retrospective study included 340 advanced NSCLC patients treated with ICIs. Cox regression analyses identified factors associated with progression-free survival (PFS). A Nutritional Inflammatory Hematological Risk Index (NIHRI) was constructed using these factors, and a prognostic nomogram was developed. Performance was assessed using the C-index, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA), with internal validation via bootstrapping. Hemoglobin and the albumin-to-alkaline phosphatase ratio (AAPR) were independent prognostic factors. The NIHRI, combining dichotomized hemoglobin (< 120 g/L vs. ≥120 g/L) and AAPR (< 0.56 vs. ≥0.56), stratified patients into low- (0 points), intermediate- (1 point), and high-risk (2 points) groups, with significantly different PFS (P<0.001). The nomogram, incorporating NIHRI, tumor stage, PD-L1, and ECOG-PS, demonstrated a C-index of 0.70 (optimism-corrected: 0.69) and predictive accuracy for 1-, 2-, and 3-year PFS (AUCs: 0.81, 0.85, and 0.88, respectively). DCA confirmed its acceptable clinical net benefit. We developed and validated a novel prognostic tool, the NIHRI, based on a combination of hemoglobin and AAPR. This integrated nomogram provides a non-invasive and clinically accessible quantitative method for predicting prognosis in patients with NSCLC undergoing immunotherapy, thereby aiding in personalized clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: An intraoperative ACTH monitoring during resection of hormone-secreting neuroendocrine neoplasms remains a subject of a debate. We present the case of a 36-year-old man with clinical and biochemical features of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism. Dynamic endocrine testing, including the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test, metyrapone test, and desmopressin stimulation test resulted in inconclusive results, precluding clear differentiation between Cushing's disease and ectopic Cushing's syndrome. Pituitary imaging revealed no definite focal lesion, whereas chest imaging detected a small pulmonary nodule along with an incidental adrenal adenoma. Taking into account rapid clinical course and the severity of clinical symptoms surgical resection of the lung lesion was undertaken with intraoperative ACTH monitoring. Due to compilation of factors patient was sent to thoracic surgery without delay. A transient ACTH surge was observed during first stage tumor excision and, even though intraoperative pathological and surgical findings indicated the complete tumor resection, which contributed to the decision to extend the procedure to an upper lobectomy, after which a marked and sustained decline in ACTH concentrations was observed. Histopathological examination confirmed a typical pulmonary carcinoid tumor, and surgical treatment resulted in clinical and biochemical remission, followed by gradual recovery of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. This case highlights the limitations of dynamic testing and imaging in ECS, particularly in indolent presentation, and underscored the potential value of intraoperative ACTH monitoring as an adjunctive tool for tumor localization and surgical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Average intensity projection (AIP) is an image generation method obtained by averaging the images of each phase of 4D-CT. This study aimed to evaluate tumor respiratory motion and, using the union of contours from all 4D-CT phases (4DTotal) as the reference, to compare contour agreement among contours derived from 3D-CT, maximum intensity projection (MIP), and AIP images. In addition, dose metrics in treatment planning were evaluated to explore the dosimetric impact of contour differences among the image sets. METHODS: Eight patients who underwent lung stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) at our institution were included. Tumor motion was first characterized from centroid positions across ten 4D-CT phases. Next, 4DTotal was generated by taking the union of the contours extracted from each phase. Finally, contours from 4D-CT AIP, 4D-CT MIP, and slow-scan 3D-CT (3DSlow) were compared with 4DTotal using volume difference, centroid difference, Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Jaccard index, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), mean surface distance (MSD), and surface Dice similarity coefficient with a 2-mm tolerance. In addition, treatment plans were generated using each contour set, and Dmax (cGy), lung V5 (%), lung V20 (%), conformity index (CI), and homogeneity index (HI) were compared. RESULTS: Tumor motion was greatest in the inferior-superior direction and was generally multi-directional. For AIP, centroid difference was ≤1 mm in each direction (LR/AP/IS), and the median values of DSC, Jaccard index, HD95, MSD, and surface DSC (2 mm) were 0.831, 0.711, 1.707 mm, 0.451 mm, and 0.981, respectively, showing good geometric agreement with 4DTotal. No significant differences were observed between AIP and MIP, whereas both AIP and MIP showed better agreement than 3DSlow. In the dose evaluation, no significant overall differences were observed for any metric among the four contour sets. In the exploratory analysis, paired comparisons using 4DTotal as the reference showed a directional decrease in lung V20 for AIP and a directional increase in CI for MIP. These findings should not be interpreted as definitive conclusions, but rather as results of an exploratory analysis based on a limited number of cases. CONCLUSION: The AIP method showed good geometric approximation to 4DTotal and may represent the time-dependent displacement of tumor position within a single dataset. In this limited exploratory analysis, no major disadvantage in treatment planning was observed. However, the observed changes in dose metrics, including lung V20, should not be interpreted as evidence of dosimetric superiority and require further validation. Because of uncertainty in the reference contour and the limited number of cases, further investigation is needed to clarify its clinical significance.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundThe widespread success of tobacco control policy and smoking cessation campaigns has led to considerable reductions in lung cancer mortality. However, it is currently not known how many more deaths might have occurred if not for the substantial progress made in lung cancer control.MethodsIn this retrospective study, we used age-specific population counts and lung cancer mortality rates from 1950 to 2019 (from 48 countries) from the Global Cancer Observatory. We estimated age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR), standardized to the WHO (2000-2025) Standard Population. Peak mortality was defined as the year when the maximum ASMR was reached for each country and sex. For each year in the period following peak mortality, the expected number of lung cancer deaths was estimated using peak-year age-specific mortality rates and age-specific population counts for that year. The number of avoided deaths was estimated as the difference between expected and observed lung cancer deaths in that period.ResultsLung cancer mortality peaked for males in all 48 countries but has yet to peak for females in 11 countries. There have been 3.08 million avoided lung cancer deaths since mortality rates peaked for many countries (2.93 million for males, 0.15 million for females). Across these countries, 21.4% and 4.3% of expected lung cancer mortality has been avoided since mortality peaked for males and females, respectively. Fourteen countries have reduced lung cancer mortality more than 25% for men, while only two countries have for women. There have been statistically significant reductions in lung cancer deaths for 46 out of 48 (96%) countries for men and 14 out of 48 (29%) countries for women.ConclusionThere has been a substantial number of lung cancer deaths avoided since mortality rates peaked for many countries, though the reduction in mortality has not been observed in all countries or equally for males and females.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality in Jordan, with most cases presenting at advanced stages. Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening has demonstrated mortality reduction in high-risk populations in developed countries. This study evaluates the feasibility and potential impact of implementing LDCT lung cancer screening in Jordan and includes a health benefit analysis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed Jordan's at-risk population using NELSON trial eligibility criteria and 2019 STEPS smoking survey data. Current radiological resources were assessed through official government sources and compared with international benchmarks from countries with established lung cancer screening programs. Health benefits were modeled using stage migration data from the NELSON trial applied to Jordan's lung cancer registry data (2013-2022) to calculate a benefit analysis. RESULTS: An estimated 622,499 Jordanians, age 50-74 years, meet screening eligibility criteria. Jordan has 37.69 radiologists per million population (PMP; range, 6.03-62.47 across governorates), compared with the modeled minimum of 65.63. CT scanner availability is 16.37 PMP, very close to the minimum requirement of 16.76 but with significant geographic disparities. Modeling suggests screening could increase stage I diagnoses from 8.38% to 35.28% and reduce stage IV diagnoses from 73% to 54%, projecting a reduction of 34.93 advanced-stage presentations annually. CONCLUSION: Although Jordan approaches adequacy in CT scanner availability, significant radiologist shortages and geographic disparities present major implementation challenges for LDCT lung cancer screening. Modeling uncertainties and infrastructure gaps necessitates pilot studies to validate assumptions before national implementation. Targeted infrastructure investment and workforce development are essential prerequisites for effective lung cancer screening in Jordan.

papers.abstract_en: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) has limited treatment options, motivating investigation of molecular pathways that support tumor-cell growth. Forkhead box D1 (FOXD1) expression was assessed using gene expression profiling interactive analysis (GEPIA), quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), western blotting, and immunohistochemistry in paired tissues and cell lines. FOXD1 or methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3) was depleted in LUSC cells, and cell viability, apoptosis, migration, global N6-methyladenosine (m6A), transcript stability, and protein stability were evaluated. A FOXD1-knockdown xenograft model tested the in vivo role of FOXD1; METTL3 was not manipulated in animals. FOXD1 expression was higher in LUSC tissues and cells than in corresponding controls. FOXD1 knockdown reduced viability and migration, increased apoptosis, and suppressed xenograft growth. METTL3 expression correlated with FOXD1 in paired LUSC tissues. In cultured cells, METTL3 knockdown lowered global m6A and FOXD1 abundance, whereas FOXD1 re-expression partially rescued the associated phenotypes. Actinomycin D, cycloheximide, and MG132 assays were consistent with METTL3-associated changes in FOXD1 RNA and protein stability. These data support a functional association between METTL3 and FOXD1 in LUSC cells. In vivo, FOXD1 knockdown suppressed xenograft growth and reduced Ki-67 staining, establishing FOXD1 as a promoter of xenograft growth. Direct METTL3-FOXD1 binding, site-specific m6A modification, reader dependence, and in vivo validation of the complete METTL3-FOXD1 pathway remain to be established.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of aumolertinib versus osimertinib as first-line treatment for advanced epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) from the perspective of the Chinese healthcare system, and to explore economic outcomes across clinically relevant subgroups. METHODS: A partitioned survival model with three health states was developed over a 10-year horizon with a 28-day cycle length. Clinical inputs were derived from indirect evidence based on the AENEAS and FLAURA trials. In the base-case analysis, the progression-free survival (PFS) effect was informed by a published simulated treatment comparison, whereas the overall survival (OS) hazard ratio for aumolertinib versus osimertinib was conservatively set at 1.00. Costs and health outcomes were discounted at 5% annually. Outcomes included total costs, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental net monetary benefit (iNMB) at a willingness-to-pay threshold of 298,995 Chinese Yuan (CNY) per QALY. One-way sensitivity, probabilistic sensitivity, scenario, threshold, and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: In the overall population, osimertinib was associated with a total cost of 193,447.40 CNY and 1.981 QALYs, whereas aumolertinib was associated with a total cost of 207,484.66 CNY and 2.000 QALYs. Compared with osimertinib, aumolertinib yielded an additional 0.019 QALYs at an additional cost of 14,037.26 CNY, resulting in an iNMB of -8,307.60 CNY. Thus, aumolertinib was not economically favorable in the base-case analysis. At the prespecified threshold, the probability of being cost-effective was 0.58 for osimertinib and 0.42 for aumolertinib. Scenario and threshold analyses showed that the results were sensitive to drug price and the comparative OS effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed differences in the direction of point estimates across subgroups, but uncertainty remained substantial across all subgroups. CONCLUSION: Under the current Chinese pricing environment and available indirect comparative evidence, aumolertinib and osimertinib showed broadly similar economic profiles as first-line treatment for advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: This case report describes a rare presentation of pulmonary melanoma of unknown primary managed through a same-day robotic diagnostic and therapeutic approach. A man in his 70s with an incidentally detected lingular pulmonary nodule suspicious for non-small cell lung cancer underwent robotic navigation bronchoscopy for biopsy and dye marking, immediately followed by robotic-assisted thoracic surgery. Intraoperative frozen section revealed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm, prompting definitive surgical resection during the same anaesthetic event. Final histopathology and molecular analysis confirmed melanoma, with no identifiable cutaneous, mucosal or ocular primary. The patient subsequently received adjuvant immunotherapy and remains disease-free at 24 months. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of pulmonary melanoma mimicking lung carcinoma and demonstrates how integration of robotic bronchoscopy and robotic surgery can enable rapid diagnosis, definitive management and streamlined care within a single operative session.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Given the potential benefit of MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) after progression on osimertinib in EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC, evaluating real-world biomarker testing and treatment sequencing is important. We report findings from a global, direct-to-physician, survey-based chart review. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Physicians treating NSCLC were surveyed regarding rebiopsy and MET testing practices and awareness of MET overexpression and/or amplification (OverExp/Amp) cutoff levels. Biomarker testing, MET OverExp/Amp quantification and treatment sequencing were assessed in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC with acquired MET OverExp/Amp after progression on first-line osimertinib, who received second-line treatment between January 2018 and December 2023 (data cutoff: April 8, 2025). RESULTS: Among 280 physicians, rebiopsy practices varied; the most commonly reported MET testing method was NGS (78%), followed by IHC (11%) and FISH (11%). Understanding of MET OverExp/Amp cutoff levels varied, with 35%-47% of physicians unaware of appropriate cutoffs. Among 367 patients (94% with MET Amp), MET alterations were mostly detected through tissue-based (58%) versus liquid-based tests (31%) or both (11%). MET alterations were detected using NGS (77%), then PCR (10%), IHC (10%), and FISH (4%). In 257 patients with MET cutoff data available, most MET Amp had gene copy numbers ≥6 (88%). MET-TKIs (29%) and EGFR-TKIs (24%) were the most common second-line treatments, followed by chemotherapy (20%). Of 193 patients with high MET levels, most received targeted treatments (MET-TKI 35%, EGFR-TKI 23%). CONCLUSION: Rebiopsy practices and knowledge of MET OverExp/Amp cutoffs varied among physicians. IHC/FISH were underutilized; however, their use should be encouraged for optimal patient identification and treatment selection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) display functional plasticity in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), but subsets linked to immune exclusion are poorly defined. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk multi-omics data to characterize neutrophil heterogeneity in LUAD. Key findings were validated by immunofluorescence co-localization and qPCR on clinical blood and isolated neutrophils. RESULTS: Neutrophils exhibited the highest scores for an EMT-associated transcriptional program and immune exclusion among all immune cell types. A distinct JUNB+ neutrophil subpopulation was spatially enriched in immune-excluded tumor regions and correlated with unfavorable prognosis. Spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between JUNB expression and neutrophil marker module scores across tissue spots (Pearson r = 0.216 and 0.205, P = 1.84 × 10^-10 and 9.06 × 10^-11). Immunofluorescence confirmed JUNB protein co-localization with CD66b+ neutrophils in LUAD tissues (54.3% ± 8.2% of CD66b+ cells JUNB +). qPCR revealed specific upregulation of JUNB mRNA in circulating neutrophils from LUAD patients, whereas no difference was observed in whole blood. CONCLUSION: This study identifies JUNB as a marker of a neutrophil state associated with immune exclusion and poor prognosis in LUAD. The neutrophil-specific upregulation of JUNB highlights its potential as a circulating biomarker for TAN-mediated immunosuppression, which warrants validation in prospective cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the roles of RPARP-AS1 and miR-10b-5p in regulating the prognosis and tumor progression of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: A total of 138 NSCLC patients were enrolled. Surgical specimens were stored in liquid nitrogen. All patients received 5 years of clinical follow-up for prognostic assessment. In addition, multivariate Cox regression analysis was conducted to identify independent factors affecting NSCLC prognosis, and gene expression levels were quantified by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assays were performed to examine cell proliferation, and transwell assays were used to assess cell migration and invasion. Furthermore, nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation experiments were conducted to localize RPARP-AS1 distribution. The interaction between RPARP-AS1 and miR-10b-5p was examined by dual luciferase reporter assays, and downstream targets in NSCLC were predicted using databases. RESULTS: RPARP-AS1 was downregulated, while miR-10b-5p was upregulated in both NSCLC patient tissues and cells. Patients with reduced RPARP-AS1 expression or increased miR-10b-5p expression had lower survival rates, accompanied by worsened tumor size, differentiation, and metastasis. oe-RPARP-AS1 inhibited tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. However, RPARP-AS1-induced functional alterations in NSCLC cells were mediated by miR-10b-5p. A total of 47 overlapping genes were identified to potentially mediate downstream signaling pathways of the RPARP-AS1/miR-10b-5p axis in NSCLC cells. CONCLUSION: Silencing RPARP-AS1 targeted miR-10b-5p to induce NSCLC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, leading to tumor progression and poor prognosis.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have enabled the clinical translation of nucleic acid therapeutics, and their composition plays a critical role in organ targeting and route-specific delivery. Intranasal (IN) administration offers direct access to the lungs, while reducing systemic exposure. However, designing LNPs capable of overcoming respiratory tract barriers remains a challenge. METHODS: We used DNA barcoding (b-DNA) for high-throughput in vivo screening of an LNP library following IN administration to investigate the impact of helper lipid identity and changes in the relative helper lipid/cholesterol composition on lung delivery. Following physicochemical characterization, pooled LNPs were administered intranasally to C57BL/6 mice, and their biodistribution was quantified by next-generation sequencing. Lead formulations were further evaluated for lung transfection in vivo and pulmonary cell transfection in vitro, cell viability, concentration-response relationships, and membrane-disruptive properties were also assessed. To better understand the discrepancies between the in vivo and in vitro performance, LNP stability was investigated in simulated nasal fluid and cell culture media. RESULTS: DOPE-based LNPs exhibited uniform diameters of approximately 90-110 nm, whereas DSPC- and DOTAP-based formulations showed greater variability in size. While DOPE- and DSPC-LNPs displayed slightly negative zeta potential values, DOTAP-formulations exhibited positive values. DSPC-LNP6 has emerged as the lead formulation for lung delivery and transfection in vivo, despite exhibiting limited transfection efficiency in pulmonary cells in vitro. Notably, the impact of simulated nasal fluid on the physicochemical properties of LNPs was comparable across formulations, suggesting that intrinsic membrane properties contribute to enhanced pulmonary transfection after IN administration. Finally, DSPC-LNP6 successfully mediated TRAIL mRNA delivery and induced tumor cell death in an experimental lung metastasis model. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings provide critical insights into the development of RNA therapeutics that target the respiratory tract.

papers.abstract_en: Targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) remains a proven strategy for the treatment of lung adenocarcinoma; however, acquired drug resistance and suboptimal long-term efficacy of the currently available EGFR inhibitors spurred the pursuit of new EGFR-targeted molecules. Hence, a series of pyridine-cored derivatives was rationally designed by strategically integrating pharmacophoric features of Gefitinib. Subsequently, the molecules were synthesised via promising synthetic approaches (Pd-catalyzed CN coupling, nucleophilic substitution reaction), and the characterized compounds (3-5 and 7a-h) were screened at the cellular level using the lung cancer cells (A549) via MTT assay. Consequently, the evaluated compounds were identified as promising leads at the cellular level. Specifically, molecule 5 exhibited potent antiproliferative activity against the A549 cells, with an IC50 value of 8.90 ± 1.6 μM, which was comparable to that of Gefitinib (IC50 = 9.22 ± 1.153 μM). Importantly, molecule 5 exhibited reduced cytotoxicity over the non-cancerous mouse fibroblast cells (L929). Moreover, mechanistic studies of molecule 5 demonstrated enhanced clonogenic survival, modulated intracellular ROS levels, substantially enhanced apoptotic cell populations, and modulation of EGFR protein expression as determined by ELISA. Notably, the combination of molecule 5 with gefitinib revealed the apparent IC50 value of 7.13 ± 0.53 μM under the specific experimental condition. On the other hand, molecular docking studies predicted the favourable binding modes with the EGFR binding sites, with predicted favourable binding affinities ranging from -7.4 to -10.3 kcal/mol. In addition, MD simulation and DFT calculations provide supportive insights into the predicted stability of the ligand-receptor complex and the electronic properties of the synthesised molecules. Collectively, molecule 5 represents as promising pyridine-based scaffold for further investigation as an anti-NSCLC lead, through additional structural modification, and further studies are required to establish its precise molecular mechanism.

papers.abstract_en: This study presents EffAtt-LungNet, an attention-guided deep learning framework for three-class lung histopathology classification. The model combines an EfficientNetB3 backbone with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to refine features and improve discrimination among benign lung tissue, lung adenocarcinoma, and lung squamous cell carcinoma. Experiments used the publicly released LC25000 lung subset, which contains 15,000 images across three classes and was itself produced by augmenting a smaller collection of underlying histopathology images. We generated 10,500 additional fixed variants, creating a balanced working corpus of 25,500 images with training, validation, and test partitions of 15,300, 2,550, and 7,650 images. EffAtt-LungNet reached 99.86% accuracy, 99.86% precision, 99.86% recall, 99.86% F1 score, and 0.9997 AUC on the image-level test partition. Performance was stable across five random seeds (mean accuracy 99.86±0.02%), and paired errors differed from those of the EfficientNetB3 backbone (McNemar's test, χ2=47.27, p < 0.001). Because pre-augmentation source identifiers for the released LC25000 images were unavailable, independence at the earliest source-image level could not be confirmed. The results therefore represent internal tile-level benchmark performance and require validation on independent, non-augmented, multi-centre datasets before any translational or clinical claim can be made.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer-related fatalistic beliefs and perceived information ambiguity may reduce engagement in cancer prevention and screening. Fatalistic beliefs reflect perceptions that cancer outcomes are inevitable despite prevention or treatment, whereas perceived information ambiguity reflects uncertainty about available health information. OBJECTIVE: This study examined associations among perceived information ambiguity, cancer-related fatalistic beliefs, and lung cancer screening (LCS) uptake among LCS-eligible adults. METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from December 2023 to February 2024. Participants were LCS-eligible adults with at least a 20 pack-year smoking history, were a current smoker or quit smoking within the past 15 years, and had no prior lung cancer history. The primary outcome was LCS uptake within the past year; predictors were cancer-related fatalistic beliefs and perceived information ambiguity. Descriptive statistics and multinomial multivariable logistic regression were used to examine associations. FINDINGS: Most participants were aged 50-64 years (n = 559, 65%), female (n = 498, 58%), White (n = 681, 79%), and insured (n = 800, 93%), and had an annual household income of $34,999 or less (n = 457, 53%). Mean pack-year smoking history was 39.4 (SD = 17.4). LCS uptake was reported within the past year by 159 (18%) participants, more than one year ago by 183 (21%) participants, and never by 521 (60%) participants. Cancer-related fatalistic beliefs were not significantly associated with LCS uptake. Participants who reported perceived information ambiguity were 37% less likely to report LCS uptake in the past year (relative risk ratio = 0.63, 95% confidence interval [0.41, 0.96]). The findings support the implementation of nursing strategies to reduce perceived information ambiguity regarding LCS.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Recent researches have revealed that histamine plays a critical role in promoting pathogenesis of cancers. However, the key histamine-related molecular signatures and their functional roles in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain largely unknown. METHODS: Differentially expressed analysis was conducted on transcriptome data to screen differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between LUAD and control (adjacent non-cancerous samples) groups. The differentially expressed histamine-related genes in LUAD were identified by intersecting DEGs and histamine-related genes. Univariate Cox regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) analyses were applied to determine key signatures associated with LUAD prognosis. Subsequently, we constructed a histamine-related prognostic risk model, compared functional enrichment and immune cell infiltration, and predicted immunotherapeutic responses and chemotherapeutic sensitivities between two risk groups using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), CIBERSORT, and TIDE algorithms. Finally, we investigated the expression patterns and methylation levels of key signatures. RESULTS: Firstly, 24 candidate histamine-related genes in LUAD, which were involved in histamine transport/secretion and neurotransmitter receptor activity were identified. After univariate Cox regression and LASSO analyses, five histamine-related genes, including SLC18A2, CDT1, PLA2G3, TSPAN7 and BTK were identified as associated with LUAD prognosis. Specifically, CDT1 was up-regulated, while the other four genes were down-regulated in LUAD samples. By calculating the histamine-related risk score, a risk model with area under curve values >0.6 (up to 0.7) for 1-, 3-, and 5-year predictions in both training and validation sets was constructed and validated. Further enrichment analysis showed a relation between risk score and immune (immune cells, immunotherapy response), and we found that low-risk group was in a more immunoactive status. Importantly, low-risk patients were predicted to have better responses to immunotherapy, while high-risk group had greater sensitivity to crizotinib, docetaxel, erlotinib, gefitinib, paclitaxel and vinorelbine. Moreover, we identified that the DNA methylation profiles of these signatures were altered in LUAD. CONCLUSION: In this study, we focused on histamine, identified histamine-related genes and developed a new prognostic model for LUAD, providing an important theoretical foundation and practical reference for pathogenesis and precision treatment of patients with LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To comprehensively evaluate respiratory-induced organ motion and deformation using volume-based analysis, overcoming the limitations of conventional point-based methods in radiation therapy for lung malignancies. MATERIAL AND METHODS: The Internal target volume (ITV) and organs at risk (OARs) were delineated on averaged-phase images from 4D-CT datasets of 11 lung cancer patients. Deformable image registration using an enhanced non-parametric algorithm generated deformation vector fields (DVFs) between each respiratory phase and a reference phase. Voxel-level displacements within each structure were statistically analyzed, quantifying ITV and OAR motion via geometric centroid displacement, mean voxel displacement, and 80th/90th percentile displacements. Pearson correlation analysis assessed the relationship between ITV motion and volumetric deformation, while one-way repeated-measures ANOVA evaluated directional consistency of OAR centroid and voxel-average displacements across LR, AP, and SI axes (p ≤0.05). RESULTS: Superior-inferior (SI) displacement of ITVs exceeded lateral and AP motion by 2-6 times. Significant centroid-voxel average motion discrepancies in the left lower lobe, right upper lobe, and diaphragm (p = 0.05) indicate limitations of point-based measures. The 80th percentile voxel motion showed potential as a centroid surrogate. Diaphragm and mediastinum deformation reached 60-80 %, with ITV deformation spanning 5-70 %. Motion metrics correlated strongly within structures but weakly with deformation. CONCLUSION: This approach enables comprehensive quantification of respiratory motion, supporting optimized motion management in lung cancer radiotherapy. As conventional metrics fail to capture organ deformation, integrating both motion and deformation assessments is essential for accurately characterizing respiratory-induced target variations.

papers.abstract_en: Lung and breast cancers are among the major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Both these cancers share several dysregulated molecular processes, including common oncogenic signaling pathways and molecular targets. Therefore, the current study focuses on the dual anticancer potential of Annona muricata. Natural products from medicinal plants are recognized as valuable sources of bioactive compounds with potential anticancer activity. In the present study, an integrated network pharmacology and in-silico approach was employed to identify potential phytoconstituents from Annona muricata against lung and breast cancers. Initially, 63 phytochemicals were collected from the IMPPAT database and screened using ADMET and toxicity prediction, resulting in nine compounds with favorable pharmacokinetic and safety profiles. Network pharmacology identified 12,321 common genes associated with both cancers, from which 209 potential targets were obtained. Protein-protein interaction analysis identified key hub genes, including HSP90AA1, MMP9, HIF1A, and MDM2, for molecular docking. Docking revealed that HIF-1α (PDB ID: 3KCX) provided the most favorable binding environment. Among the screened phytochemicals, (-)-Coreximine showed the strongest interaction with HIS199 and ASP201. MM-GBSA confirmed its highest binding affinity (-39.47 kcal/mol), while DFT and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stability and persistent binding. Overall, these computational findings suggest that (-)-Coreximine may attenuate cancer progression through modulation of HIF-1α-associated pathways and represents a promising natural lead for further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the benefit-finding experiences of female caregivers of patients with lung cancer, focusing particularly on their positive psychological adaptations throughout the caregiving process. The findings are expected to inform the development of more targeted and effective nursing interventions. METHODS: A qualitative phenomenological approach was employed, with sample size determined by the principle of data saturation. From November to December 2024, 12 female caregivers of hospitalized lung cancer patients were purposively recruited from a tertiary hospital in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. Data were collected through semistructured, in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method. MAXQDA 22.0 software was utilized to facilitate data organization, coding, and thematic analysis. RESULTS: Twelve participants aged 30-75 years were included in the study. Analysis of the interview data generated four major themes and six subthemes: (1) reflections on the meaning of life (drawing strength in adversity, reconstructing life meaning), (2) enhancement of caregiving competence (improved disease-related knowledge, strengthened caregiving role), (3) multifaceted support (perceived family support, perceived social support), and (4) adoption of positive coping strategies. CONCLUSION: Female caregivers of patients with lung cancer demonstrated clear benefit-finding experiences throughout the caregiving process. These findings underscore the importance of supporting caregivers in developing adaptive coping strategies, strengthening caregiving skills, and addressing both the physical and psychological needs of patients. Facilitating positive psychological adjustment and mobilizing supportive resources can not only promote patient self-management and well-being but also enhance caregivers' perceived benefits and reduce caregiving stress.

papers.abstract_en: In its 20-year history, the Journal of Thoracic Oncology (JTO) has published many major articles that have had a profound impact on the pathology of thoracic malignancies. One reason JTO has had such a great influence on thoracic oncology is the visionary leadership of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC), which emphasizes an international, multidisciplinary approach across all its endeavors. JTO is one of the most important initiatives of the IASLC, and its global scope, encompassing all specialties, has enabled many pathologists to play a important role in the journal. This is reflected in the participation of multiple pathologists on the editorial board and in the prioritization of publishing impactful articles led by pathologists. This has been a good investment for JTO and IASLC, because eight of the top 20 most cited articles in the journal in the past 20 years were led by pathologists. This article reviews the many advances published in JTO, most of which concern lung cancer, mesothelioma, thymic tumors, and cardiac tumors. During this period, many breakthroughs occurred in surgical pathology, small biopsy and cytology, management of lung cancer after neoadjuvant therapy, molecular genetics, and biomarker testing. Many of these advances have had a direct impact on patient care, providing new ways to stratify patients for therapeutic management decisions.
