papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies. DESIGN: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial. SETTING: 18 Dutch community hospitals. PARTICIPANTS: Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. INTERVENTIONS: Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies. RESULTS: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24). CONCLUSIONS: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice. TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl; NL-OMON25059 (prospective registration; 4 Dec 2019).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The tumor microenvironment exerts intense survival pressure on CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), yet the cellular basis for an earlier, less-exhausted state associated with response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. We previously identified BCL2A1 as a CD8+ TIL-derived marker predictive of a response to PD-1 blockade. Here we combine deep single-cell discovery with experimental validation in primary human T cells to characterise the BCL2A1-associated CD8+ TIL state and its candidate upstream signal. METHODS: We integrated four transcriptomic cohorts-pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq with CD8+ TIL deconvolution (n=60), on-treatment scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=11), longitudinal scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=18), and an independent post-treatment cohort (n=59)-with in silico perturbation, pathway, and metabolic-flux analyses, and experimentally tested a key prediction of this state by flow cytometry in primary human CD8+ T cells. RESULTS: BCL2A1 high CD8+ TILs showed elevated BCL2A1 expression without coordinated upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family genes, maintained minimal exhaustion, and occupied an early, BCL6-, TCF7-, and NFKB1-regulated pseudotime state. Across longitudinal and post-treatment cohorts, they formed diverse, low-expansion repertoires rather than dominant expanded clones, with reduced biosynthetic flux (branched-chain amino acid and purine metabolism) consistent with a non-proliferative state. NF-κB signaling was elevated, and TNF-α was nominated as the leading candidate upstream ligand of BCL2A1. We then experimentally tested this prediction: in primary human CD8+ T cells, TNF-α induced BCL2A1 protein ≈13-fold (44.5% vs. 3.4% BCL2A1+; MFI 2.93-fold; P < 0.0001), whereas CD3/CD28 activation alone did not, establishing a TNF-α-specific, protein-level response. CONCLUSIONS: Combining integrative single-cell analysis with experimental validation in primary human T cells, we define BCL2A1 as a marker of an early, less-exhausted CD8+ TIL state associated with improved ICB outcomes in NSCLC; a survival-related role is supported by these associations but was not functionally tested.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are being investigated in advanced small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the evidence is dominated by early-phase studies conducted in non-exchangeable treatment settings. We evaluated the activity and toxicity of ADCs while separating later-line monotherapy from frontline combination therapy, later-line combination therapy, and post-induction maintenance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception and in 28 August 2026. ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) were searched on 28 August 2026. We constructed an arm-level dataset that recorded regimen, dose, clinical context, target, outcome definition, numerator, denominator, analysis set, and source. The primary quantitative synthesis was restricted to second-line or later ADC monotherapy; other clinical contexts were summarized descriptively. Single-arm proportions were synthesized using a binomial-normal random-intercept generalized linear mixed model on the logit scale. We reported 95% confidence intervals (CIs), between-study variance, heterogeneity, and 95% prediction intervals. An inverse-variance logit random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp inference was used as a sensitivity analysis. Fixed-time Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and inconsistently defined common adverse events were not pooled. RESULTS: 16 trial families evaluating eight ADCs across five target classes met the eligibility criteria. In the primary later-line monotherapy analysis, the pooled ORR was 25.7% (95% CI, 16.4%-37.9%), and the pooled DCR was 72.7% (95% CI, 60.7%-82.2%). The pooled incidences of grade ≥3 TEAEs and grade ≥3 TRAEs were 62.8% (95% CI, 59.6%-65.9%) and 45.5% (95% CI, 35.5%-56.0%), respectively. The prediction intervals for ORR, DCR, and grade ≥3 TRAEs were wide. Proportions observed in a new study may therefore differ substantially from the pooled estimates. Frontline combinations, later-line combinations, and maintenance therapy yielded context-specific signals but were not compared with later-line monotherapy. Target-stratified analyses were exploratory; B7-H3 and DLL3 estimates were based on small, non-comparative groups, whereas Trop-2 and SEZ6 were not pooled because fewer than three studies were available. CONCLUSIONS: Later-line ADC monotherapy showed antitumor activity but frequent clinically important toxicity, with substantial between-study variation. The evidence does not establish superiority by treatment line, regimen, agent, or molecular target; single-arm response estimates also do not demonstrate a survival benefit. Randomized, context-specific trials using harmonized efficacy and safety definitions are needed.

METHODS: Jazz EMERGE 402 was a prospective, observational, phase 4 trial (NCT04894591) that evaluated lurbinectedin for previously treated SCLC in a diverse, real-world population. RESULTS: As of July 17, 2025, 267 patients received ≥ 1 lurbinectedin dose. At baseline, the median age was 67 years, 52 (19%) patients had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group score ≥ 2, 67 (25%) had brain metastases, and 88 (33%) had platinum-resistant disease. ORR (95% confidence interval [CI]) was 29% (23%-36%) overall (n = 189) and 33% (25%-42%) in second-line treatment (n = 118). Patients with brain metastases had lower ORR (17% vs 32% without; odds ratio, 0.28 [95% CI: 0.10-0.76]). Median (95% CI) PFS and OS were 3.3 (2.6-4.1) and 7.6 (6.4-8.7) months. OS was shorter with platinum-resistant vs platinum-sensitive disease (5.8 vs 9.3 months; hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI: 1.17-2.28]). Eighty-eight (33%) patients had treatment-related adverse events, including anemia (8%) and neutropenia (7%); 21 (8%) discontinued treatment due to adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: In a broad, real-world population with previously treated SCLC, lurbinectedin was associated with clinically meaningful effectiveness and predictable and manageable safety. Lower ORR and OS were seen in patients with brain metastases and platinum-resistant disease, respectively.

papers.abstract_en: Lymph nodes (LNs), principal sites of antitumor immunity, may undergo immune-mediated regression; whether neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT)-induced regression indicates prognosis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We aimed to establish and validate a lymph node regression grade (LNRG) system for prognostic stratification. This multicenter, retrospective cohort study analyzed 965 patients receiving PD-1-based NCIT and surgery at three Chinese tertiary cancer centers. LNRG was the ratio of summed viable tumor area to summed bed area (residual viable plus regressed preexisting tumor) across all dissected LNs. Negative LNs were assigned LNRG 0. Survival and predictive performance were assessed using Kaplan-Meier/Cox regression, time-dependent area under the curve, Brier score, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Overall, 28,882 LNs were evaluated; patients were classified as LNRG 0-4 in 385 (39.9%), 150 (15.5%), 26 (2.7%), 141 (14.6%), and 263 (27.3%), respectively. LNRG independently predicted disease-free and overall survival, with Grades 1-2 conferring the most favorable outcomes and Grade 4 the poorest. A random survival forest model incorporating LNRG, tumor regression grade, ypAJCC stage, and perineural invasion predicted 2-year disease-free survival in training and external validation cohorts. LNRG is a novel, independent prognostic indicator after NCIT.

papers.abstract_en: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are pivotal orchestrators of immune evasion, yet the functional significance of the calcineurin signaling pathway in TAM plasticity remains elusive. Analyzing TCGA Lung Cancer datasets and clinical samples, we identified PPP3CA as the major calcineurin catalytic subunit in TAMs, whose downregulation correlates with poor patient survival and tumor progression. Myeloid-specific Ppp3ca knockout in mice accelerated tumor growth, reducing anti-tumor M1-like macrophages and CD8+ T cells while enriching pro-tumor M2-like TAMs. In vitro assays confirmed that Ppp3ca deficiency impaired the polarization of TAMs toward the M1 type. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that PPP3CA-mediated regulation of TAM plasticity is dependent on the NF-κB signaling pathway, as Ppp3ca loss significantly blunted NF-κB activation. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of calcineurin using cyclosporin A (CsA) effectively recapitulated the myeloid-deficient phenotype, shifting TAMs toward a pro-tumorigenic M2 state and promoting tumor malignancy, providing an experimental explanation for the elevated cancer risk associated with clinical calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) use. Collectively, our findings identify the PPP3CA-NF-κB axis as a pivotal regulator of macrophage plasticity and provide a high-value translational basis for targeting this pathway to remodel the TME in lung cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of tislelizumab combined with nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and its effects on serum tumor markers and inflammatory cytokines. METHODS: A total of 228 advanced ESCC patients were retrospectively enrolled and divided into an observation group (tislelizumab combined with nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin, n=114) and a control group (chemotherapy alone: nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin, n=114). Related serological indicators, T lymphocyte subsets, quality of life, short-term efficacy, pathological response, survival outcomes and adverse reactions were compared. Independent prognostic factors were analyzed via univariate and multivariate Cox regression. RESULTS: After treatment, both groups exhibited decreased levels of tumor markers, inflammatory cytokines, soluble PD-1, PD-L1, VEGF and MMP-9, with lower levels in the observation group (all P<0.05). The observation group had improved immune function, higher SF-36 scores, as well as higher objective response rate, disease control rate, and pathological response indexes (all P<0.05). Moreover, patients in the observation group had longer progression-free survival and overall survival (both P<0.05). Advanced TNM stage was an adverse prognostic factor, while combined immunochemotherapy reduced mortality risk. CONCLUSION: Tislelizumab plus the dual chemotherapy regimen can effectively reduce serum tumor markers and alleviate tumor-related inflammation, improve immune status, quality of life and survival of patients with advanced ESCC with acceptable safety, supporting its potential for broader clinical application.

papers.abstract_en: Non-SMC condensin I complex subunit G (NCAPG) is implicated in tumor progression and TGF-β pathway activation, yet its roles in oncogenesis and immune modulation within the lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) microenvironment remain largely unexplored. Here, we used bioinformatics analysis to identify key upregulated genes in LUSC and assessed the effects of NCAPG and its upstream regulator E2F transcription factor 8 (E2F8) on malignant phenotypes via gain- and loss-of-function assays in NCI-H226 and NCI-H1703 LUSC cell lines, with in vivo efficacy validated using KLN205 cell isografts and NTCU-induced primary LUSC mouse models. Neutrophil polarization, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and CD8⁺ T cell cytotoxicity was analyzed in co-culture systems and tumor tissues. Arundanine was identified as a potential NCAPG inhibitor via molecular docking and tested as monotherapy or in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy. We found that NCAPG was significantly upregulated in LUSC, and NCAPG depletion markedly impaired LUSC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. Mechanistically, NCAPG activated TGF-β signaling, which drove pro-tumor N2 neutrophil polarization and induced NETosis; these NETs upregulated PD-L1 expression on tumor cells and suppressed the expansion and cytotoxic function of CD8⁺ T cells. E2F8 was found to transcriptionally activate NCAPG by directly binding to its promoter. Furthermore, Arundanine destabilized NCAPG protein, suppressed TGF-β-mediated NET formation, and potentiated anti-PD-1 therapy to significantly prolong survival in LUSC models. Collectively, the E2F8/NCAPG axis promotes LUSC progression by orchestrating a TGF-β-driven immunosuppressive microenvironment, and targeting NCAPG with Arundanine represents a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion and sensitize LUSC to PD-1 blockade.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study is to evaluate the application, methodology and consistency of utility values used in National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) single technology appraisals (STAs) of targeted therapies for advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) over the past decade. METHODS: A review was conducted of NICE STAs of NSCLC targeted therapies from 2012 to 2022, focusing on four key aspects: (1) utility values per health state as defined by the economic model structure; 2) the primary sources of these utility values; (3) the methods used to derive utilities for quality of life, and 4) the application of disutilities or utility decrements. RESULTS: In the included 16 appraisals for targeted therapies, substantial variation was identified in the application, methodology, and consistency of utility values used in CUAs appraised by NICE over the past decade. Most appraisals used health state-specific utilities, with progression free values primarily derived from clinical trials and progressed disease values more often derived from external literature. Disutilities for adverse events were applied in an inconsistent way and no stratification by age was reported. CONCLUSION: Enhancing methodological consistency and incorporating up-to-date, representative utility data, particularly for progressed disease and adverse events, would strengthen the robustness, transparency and comparability of NICE technology appraisals of targeted therapies in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Anti-angiogenic therapies provide clinically meaningful benefit in selected treatment settings for advanced non-small cell lung cancer, but durable responses are limited by heterogeneous and adaptive resistance. This resistance is not solely tumor-intrinsic; it emerges from interactions among tumor plasticity, compensatory angiogenic signaling, hypoxia, stromal and immune remodeling, vascular recovery, and alternative blood-supply mechanisms. These processes require different biological variables and therefore cannot be adequately interrogated by a single experimental model. Patient-derived lung cancer organoids preserve patient-specific tumor features and are useful for studying tumor-intrinsic responses, but tumor-only organoids do not reproduce perfusion-dependent vascular physiology, permeability, or drug-delivery dynamics. Microenvironment-integrated co-culture, vascularization, and microfluidic or perfusion engineering can extend these capabilities, although model complexity alone does not establish stronger evidence. This review integrates the clinical and mechanistic basis of anti-angiogenic resistance with the capabilities and limitations of current lung cancer organoid models and other three-dimensional systems. We propose a mechanism-matched framework linking the resistance mechanism to the required variable, the minimum set of model capabilities, and claim-matched readouts. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing structural from functional vascularization, tumor drug response from anti-angiogenic resistance, and acute treatment effects from acquired resistance. Current lung cancer organoid systems can model tumor-intrinsic and selected microenvironment-mediated responses and, increasingly, vascular responses, but direct longitudinal evidence of acquired anti-angiogenic resistance remains limited. Future progress will depend on fit-for-purpose standardization, functional qualification, longitudinal modeling, and prospective alignment with clinically observed resistance trajectories.

papers.abstract_en: This study examined the association of surgical approach with operative and postoperative outcomes as well as margin and nodal outcomes after complex segmentectomy, comparing mini-thoracotomy (MT) with multiportal minimally invasive thoracic surgery (mMITS) and, within mMITS, video-assisted thoracic surgery (mVATS) with multiportal robot-assisted thoracic surgery (mRATS), using propensity score matching (PSM). The study cohort comprised 808 consecutive patients treated with complex segmentectomy for suspected malignant pulmonary tumors from January 2015 through July 2026. Of these, 138 underwent MT and 670 mMITS, including 605 mVATS and 65 mRATS. PSM (1:2) was performed for MT versus mMITS (n = 126 vs. 252) and mVATS versus mRATS (n = 126 vs. 63). We assessed operative outcomes, postoperative complications, pain-related outcomes only for the mVATS-mRATS comparison, and margin and nodal outcomes. Blood loss was lower with mMITS than with MT (5 vs. 20 mL, p < 0.001), and chest tube duration was shorter (p = 0.002). Margin and nodal outcomes did not differ significantly between MT and mMITS. mRATS was associated with less blood loss than mVATS (3 vs. 5 mL, p = 0.006), a shorter duration of regular oral analgesic use (20 vs. 31 days, p = 0.007), and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields (hilar, p = 0.037; mediastinal, p = 0.025). For complex segmentectomy, mMITS was associated with less blood loss and shorter chest tube duration than MT, without significant differences in margin and nodal outcomes. Within mMITS, mRATS was associated with shorter regular oral analgesic use and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields than mVATS.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature has been associated with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but evidence on seasonal lag patterns and susceptible populations remains limited. We characterized lag-specific and cumulative temperature-AECOPD associations during cold and warm seasons. METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort (2006-2019), we conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study with referent days matched by year, season, and day of the week. Cold-season exposure was defined as 2-m air temperature (November-April), and warm-season exposure as wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT; May-October). Conditional quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models estimated lag-specific and cumulative relative risks (RRs) over 0-28 days, adjusting for season-specific meteorological variables, PM10, PM2.5, and public holidays. Effect modification by age, sex, smoking, and body mass index (BMI) was examined. RESULTS: Among 5981 AECOPD events, lower cold-season temperatures were associated with delayed, sustained risk increases over lag days 6-23, peaking at lag 14-18 (RR = 1.23; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04-1.46). Higher warm-season WBGTs were associated with an immediate increase, peaking at lag 0-1 (RR = 1.06; 95% CI 1.02-1.10), which attenuated within 1 week. Cumulative exposure-response curves were monotonic for cold-season temperature and inverted U-shaped for warm-season WBGT. Associations were stronger in men, older adults, smokers, and those with a BMI ≥25. CONCLUSION: Cold- and warm-season ambient temperature metrics showed distinct temporal associations with AECOPD, delayed in the cold season and immediate in the warm season. Associations appeared relatively stronger among older adults, men, smokers, and individuals with higher BMI.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of first-line third-generation EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) combined with pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced lung adenocarcinoma and brain parenchymal metastases. METHODS: A bicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 150 eligible patients were enrolled and balanced by 1:1 propensity score matching. Tumor response, survival outcomes, and treatment-related adverse events were compared between groups. RESULTS: After matching, 60 patients were assigned to each group. The intracranial objective response rate was 78.3% in the combination group versus 61.7% in the monotherapy group (P = 0.046). The median intracranial progression-free survival was 28.3 months in the combination group (hazard ratio = 0.536, 95% confidence interval: 0.350-0.820, P = 0.002). Systemic progression-free survival and overall survival were also significantly prolonged in the combination arm. Adverse events were predominantly chemotherapy-related toxicities and were generally manageable. CONCLUSION: First-line third-generation EGFR-TKI plus pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy is associated with superior intracranial and systemic survival benefits in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma patients with brain parenchymal metastases, with a favorable safety profile. This study provides real-world evidence to support clinical treatment decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are emerging therapeutic options for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after the development of resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs). However, the founding EGFR alteration alone does not guide ADC selection. At progression, actionable resistance mechanisms, altered antigen expression, central nervous system (CNS) involvement, spatial heterogeneity, and histological transformation may shift treatment priorities. This narrative review links agent-specific evidence boundaries to an eight-domain assessment of the post-progression disease state and distinguishes ADC eligibility from therapeutic priority. The framework first identifies clinical scenarios requiring immediate local, CNS-directed, or lineage-specific treatment. It then evaluates resistance-directed therapy and other systemic options in the context of prior treatment. Finally, each ADC is assessed according to its evidence base, biomarkers, construct fit, disease distribution, availability, and patient-specific safety. Currently, selected TROP2-directed ADCs have the most mature evidence. HER3-directed therapy remains under investigation, whereas c-Met- and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-directed ADCs may be relevant in biomarker-defined settings. Tissue biopsy, plasma circulating tumor DNA analysis, and selected cerebrospinal fluid testing should be considered when the findings could alter clinical management. Accordingly, ADCs should be positioned relative to competing local and systemic strategies rather than considered a uniform post-osimertinib class. Prospective validation is required to determine whether this framework improves treatment outcomes.

ROS1 fusions are oncogenic drivers in a range of cancers and are identified in approximately 1-2% of NSCLCs. Zidesamtinib potently inhibits diverse ROS1 fusion proteins and clinically relevant ROS1 resistance mutations. Further, zidesamtinib has been shown to induce intracranial tumour regression in xenograft models. This article summarises the milestones in the development of zidesamtinib leading to this first approval for advanced ROS1-positive NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The acute inpatient symptom state following oesophagectomy is multidimensional and heterogeneous. However, the structure, between-patient heterogeneity, and network features of symptoms remain incompletely characterised. METHOD: We analysed 1047 postoperative patients with oesophageal cancer from four hospitals in Anhui Province, China, in the "Be Resilient to Oesophageal Cancer" program. We applied principal component analysis to summarise symptom dimensions and latent profile analysis to derive patient groups of symptom burden. Symptom networks were estimated and centrality computed to identify candidate targets. We then performed in silico node-perturbation simulations to estimate potential system-level effects of alleviating versus aggravating individual symptoms. RESULTS: Four symptom dimensions emerged from the principal component analysis: somatic discomfort and fatigue, psychological distress, social functioning impairment, and gastrointestinal/appetite-related symptoms. A low-burden group (80.2%) and a high-burden group (19.8%) were identified. The overall network's most central symptom was "reduced social interaction" (r = 2.52). Within groups, "worry" was most central in the low-burden group (r = 2.08), whereas "incision pain" was most central in the high-burden group (r=2.56). Computer simulations revealed that, within alleviating interventions, somatic symptoms accounted for the highest proportion across all symptom types (incision pain: -20.68% to -9.17%). Conversely, within aggravating interventions, psychosocial symptoms constituted the largest share in both the overall symptom network and the low-burden group (helplessness: 24.13% to 30.27%), whereas somatic symptoms dominated the high-burden group (incision pain: 9.17%). CONCLUSION: A multimethod pipeline identified reduced social interaction, worry, and incision pain as profile-specific, structurally prominent symptoms within the postoperative day 3 symptom networks. These findings highlight distinct psychosocial and somatic features across symptom-burden profiles and provide hypotheses for subsequent longitudinal and interventional studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare mediastinal tumors classified according to the WHO classification system. Classification can be challenging due to overlapping histological features. Subtyping on biopsy specimens is often inaccurate due to tumor heterogeneity and sampling effect. Since 2012 an international thymic tumor pathology expert panel is available in the Netherlands. This study evaluates the added value of this panel by assessing the discrepancies in diagnosis, inter-observer agreement and concordance on diagnosis between biopsy and the subsequent resection specimen. METHODS: All pathology excerpts from 2012 until 2024 for patients diagnosed with a thymic tumor were extracted from the national PALGA database and evaluated for histological subtype, assessment and the thymoma panel result. RESULTS: In total 1163 resection and 304 biopsy specimens were included, of which 36.1% were submitted to the thymoma panel. The diagnosis changed in 15.7% of cases after assessment. The subtypes AB and Bmix were most often submitted to the thymoma panel and the diagnosis changed most often for subtype A, B3 or Bmix. In 72.8% the concordance between the panel members exceeded 90%. The biopsy diagnosis varied from the resection diagnosis in 46.8%, but the differentiation between thymoma and thymic carcinoma was accurate on biopsy. CONCLUSION: A panel of dedicated pathologists with experience in thymic abnormalities contributed substantially to a more accurate classification of TETs, thereby guiding optimal treatment planning and prognostic evaluation. Despite the discrepancies between biopsy and resection specimens, distinguishing thymoma from thymic carcinoma was accurate on biopsy.

papers.abstract_en: Radioresistance severely compromises radiotherapy efficacy for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the intrinsic heterogeneity of cellular radioresponses among isogenic tumor cells remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing (scATAC-seq) to dissect the transcriptional and regulatory landscape underlying heterogeneous radioresponses in single-cell-derived LUAD cells following 6 Gy γ-ray irradiation. We found that isogenic LUAD cells harbored intrinsic molecular determinants for divergent radiosensitivity and displayed heterogeneous radioresponsiveness upon irradiation. A radiation-associated transcriptional cell state, coupled with DNA damage repair, apoptosis, and cell cycle regulation, emerged at 6 h post-irradiation. Inhibition of lysine demethylase 4B (KDM4B) enhanced LUAD radiosensitivity by intensifying DNA damage, whereas reduced expression of cyclin B1 (CCNB1) and DNA topoisomerase IIα (TOP2A) potentially contributed to radiation-triggered G2/M arrest. Notably, the radiation-associated regulatory cell state emerged earlier than radiation-induced transcriptional cell state. RNA polymerase II subunit A (POLR2A) functioned as a core regulator in high-responsive LUAD cells. Based on these findings, we proposed a hypothesis for the radiosensitization of LUAD cells. Collectively, this study provides multilayer mechanistic insights into LUAD radioresponse heterogeneity and yields actionable molecular candidates for developing improved radiosensitization strategies to advance precise radiotherapy for LUAD.

papers.ai_note: FVC终点仅作“描述性汇总”，未给出合并效应量、置信区间或等效性检验，所谓“一致减缓”“有利信号”缺乏可量化支撑；“无等效性证据”被表述为治疗间差异的依据，逻辑上属不确定性。吡非尼酮死亡OR 0.50并非本研究统一提取的试验级合并结果，而是引用已发表ASCEND/CAPACITY合并数据加日本3期试验，来源异质、缺乏预设分析方案，存在选择性纳入与事后汇总风险。标题与结论以“Beyond FVC”为卖点，实质将次要终点（治疗终止、死亡）置于与主要终点同等甚至更高的解释权重，且无头对头或校正后的间接比较，不能支持治疗间排序。吸入曲前列尼尔“有利FVC信号”未报告数值，无法核验。

pico.ic: 干预：抗纤维化导向治疗（吡非尼酮、尼达尼布、吸入曲前列尼尔等，含/不含背景抗纤维化治疗）；对照：安慰剂

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Phase 3 evidence for antifibrotic-directed therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) has expanded, but direct head-to-head trials are lacking. Forced vital capacity (FVC) decline remains the principal trial outcome, although it may not fully capture clinically relevant differences among therapies. METHODS: We systematically reviewed phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials of antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. FVC effects versus placebo were descriptively summarized using standardized 48-52-week estimates. All-cause treatment discontinuation and all-cause mortality were analyzed using placebo-controlled odds ratios. Sensitivity analyses assessed follow-up duration, background antifibrotic therapy, and trial-level consistency. RESULTS: Ten trials including 5,386 randomized participants were included. Pirfenidone and nintedanib showed consistent reductions in FVC decline versus placebo. Inhaled treprostinil showed a favorable FVC signal in the combined TETON-1/2 evidence, largely as add-on therapy with background antifibrotic treatment. Without background antifibrotic therapy, several therapies showed directionally favorable but imprecise FVC effects, without evidence of equivalence. Nintedanib and inhaled treprostinil were associated with higher odds of all-cause treatment discontinuation versus placebo: OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.02-1.88) and OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.08-1.78), respectively. Pirfenidone was the only therapy associated with lower odds of all-cause mortality (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.31-0.83), based on published pooled ASCEND/CAPACITY mortality data and the Japanese phase 3 trial. CONCLUSIONS: FVC decline remains essential but may not fully distinguish antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. Integrating FVC effects, background therapy, treatment continuation, and mortality provides a cautious, context-dependent framework for interpreting expanding phase 3 evidence.

papers.abstract_en: Chemoresistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the epigenetic mechanisms underlying platinum resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that Jumonji C domain-containing protein 5 (JMJD5) promotes platinum resistance in NSCLC cells and xenograft tumors while inducing a slow-proliferative, mesenchymal-like phenotype characterized by enhanced migration, invasion, spheroid formation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Mechanistically, JMJD5 interacted with RCC1 domain-containing protein 1 (RCCD1), and cisplatin treatment promoted their nuclear accumulation concomitant with reduced H3K36me2 levels. RCCD1 depletion attenuated JMJD5-associated H3K36me2 demethylation and reversed EMT-associated phenotypes and cisplatin resistance, supporting RCCD1 as a functional cofactor of JMJD5-mediated chromatin remodeling. Fibronectin 1 (FN1) was further identified as a downstream effector of this pathway. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of FN1 suppressed JMJD5-induced migration and invasion and restored cisplatin sensitivity. Notably, JMJD5-dependent FN1 protein accumulation required ongoing protein synthesis without a corresponding increase in FN1 mRNA, suggesting post-transcriptional regulation. Consistently, elevated FN1 expression was associated with unfavorable overall survival in patients with lung cancer. Collectively, these findings reveal a JMJD5-RCCD1-H3K36me2-FN1 regulatory axis linking chemotherapy-induced epigenetic remodeling to EMT-associated platinum resistance and suggest that disruption of this pathway may represent a potential strategy for overcoming chemoresistance in NSCLC.

papers.authors: Angelicola S, Frascino M, Chillico IC, Michel PLS, Pistone D, Semprini MS, Pittino OM, Ardizzoni A et al.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have transformed the treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), yet durable responses remain limited to a minority of patients. Tumor plasticity is increasingly recognized as a determinant of immunotherapy resistance, although the tumor-intrinsic contribution of immunomodulatory mediators such as IFN-γ and PD-L1 remains poorly understood. In this review, we examine emerging evidence that IFN-γ and PD-L1, beyond their established roles in tumor-immune interactions, may contribute to the regulation of NSCLC plasticity. IFN-γ can activate non-canonical programs involving dose-dependent ICAM1/PI3K/AKT/Notch1 signaling, BCAT1- and FGF2/β-catenin-mediated metabolic reprogramming, and a putative autocrine TBX21/IL-4 signaling circuit that may sustain stem-like properties. PD-L1, in turn, is functionally integrated into plasticity-associated pathways involving the TGF-β signaling axis, β-catenin stabilization, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-associated microRNA networks, YAP/TAZ, CD44 and ATM signaling, as well as TRAF6/BECN1/NF-κB-dependent regulation of autophagy. Collectively, these findings support a role for IFN-γ and PD-L1 as context-dependent modulators of NSCLC plasticity, with potential implications for immunotherapy resistance, and provide a rationale for further exploring combinatorial treatment strategies and patient stratification approaches.

papers.abstract_en: Golgin-45 (G45) is a coiled-coil protein that transits reversibly between the Golgi and nucleus. In the Golgi, G45 serves as a tether for effectors of a pro-tumorigenic secretory program, but its nuclear role remains unclear. Here, we report that, upon entering the nucleus, G45 functions as a basic leucine zipper transcription factor. From genomic mapping, RNA-sequencing, and functional validation studies, we identify G45-binding sites and show that nuclear G45 can function as a transcriptional activator or repressor, a versatility enabled by phase separation into nuclear bodies enriched in transcriptional co-regulators. In lung cancer models, Golgi-docking reinforces, whereas nuclear translocation opposes, pro-tumorigenic activity of G45. Nuclear G45 incorporates into dimeric transcription factors that silence pro-tumorigenic secreted cargos. Epigenetic events in lung cancer degrade nuclear G45 and sequester G45 in the Golgi, which unleashes malignant secretion. Thus, inter-organelle transitions govern a G45-dependent secretory axis that drives lung cancer progression.

papers.abstract_en: To investigate the local control and safety of adding high-dose-rate intraluminal brachytherapy (HDR-ILBT) with novel balloon applicator (BRAXX) after concurrent chemoradiation (CCRT) for non-surgery patients with esophageal cancer. The study enrolled 178 patients with esophageal cancer. A total of 13 patients were prospectively recruited to receive HDR-ILBT after CCRT and compared with two standard-of-care cohorts treated between 2022 and 2024. Brachytherapy was delivered via the BRAXX balloon applicator (Taiwan Food and Drug Administration approval No. 006603) using an Iridium-192 Nucletron remote afterloading system (Elekta, Stockholm, Sweden). The primary endpoint was freedom from local tumor recurrence (FFLTR). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), disease progression-free survival (DPFS), and toxicities. Sankey diagrams and swimmer plot were utilized to visualize the longitudinal tumor response dynamics and individual survival trajectories. The median follow-up was 25.2 months. The 1-year and 2-year FFLTR rates were 93.3% and 81.2% (nCCRT + surgery), 84.6% and 67.7% (CCRT + ILBT), and 62.5% and 52.9% (dCCRT alone), respectively (P < 0.001). Consistent survival improvements were observed in both OS and DPFS in CCRT + ILBT cohort. Sankey diagrams demonstrated a favorable dynamic evolution in treatment response within the CCRT + ILBT cohort, achieving a clinical complete response (cCR) rate of 61.5% and overall response rate (ORR) of 69.2% at the end of per-protocol 1-year follow-up. Swimmer plot illustrated that response conversion and consolidation translated into long-term survival. The addition of HDR-ILBT did not exacerbate treatment-related esophageal strictures or fistula formations necessitating intervention. The addition of HDR-ILBT utilizing BRAXX applicator following CCRT is a feasible and promising strategy to enhance local control and prolong survival for non-surgical patients with esophageal cancer. By leveraging its distinct dosimetric advantages and streamlined workflow, ILBT holds the potential to consolidate disease-free status and eradicate residual disease. Further validation through large-scale, prospective clinical trials is still warranted to confirm its clinical benefit and long-term safety. If further validated, this strategy could offer a meaningful addition to the current treatment paradigm.

papers.abstract_en: Although single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy is increasingly adopted for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), evidence comparing its long-term oncological efficacy with that of the two-port approach remains scarce. This propensity score-matched study evaluated perioperative outcomes, postoperative recovery, and 3-year survival following single-port versus two-port thoracoscopic lobectomy in patients with NSCLC. We retrospectively analyzed 167 consecutive patients (single-port, n = 82; two-port, n = 85); propensity score matching (1:1, caliper = 0.2) yielded 72 matched pairs. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative pain (VAS), inflammatory markers (CRP, PCT, IL-1β), pulmonary function, 30-day complications, 3-year overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and multivariable Cox regression were compared. Following matching, the single-port group demonstrated significantly longer operative time (187.3 ± 56.4 vs. 142.2 ± 49.4 minutes; P<0.001) but reduced blood loss (96.5 ± 42.0 vs. 121.7 ± 48.1 mL; P<0.001) 24-hour chest drainage volume (632.3 ± 447.3 vs. 945.5 ± 501.3 mL; P<0.001), and incision length (3.57 ± 1.37 vs. 4.94 ± 1.52 cm; P<0.001). Lymph node yield did not differ significantly (17.3 ± 4.1 vs. 16.1 ± 3.6; P = 0.058). Postoperative VAS scores were significantly lower in the single-port group on days 3, 5, and 7 (all P<0.001), with attenuated inflammatory responses (lower CRP, PCT, and IL-1β; all P<0.001) and better pulmonary function recovery (higher PaO2, SpO2, FVC, and FEV1; all P<0.05). Thirty-day complication rates did not differ significantly (6.9% vs. 9.7%; P = 0.763). Over a median follow-up of 38 months, 3-year OS (86.5% vs. 84.4%; P = 0.572) and 3-year DFS (79.2% vs. 77.1%; P = 0.684) were comparable. Multivariable analysis identified pathological stage II (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.35-4.43; P = 0.003) and lymphovascular invasion (HR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.18-3.72; P = 0.012) as independent predictors of poorer DFS, whereas surgical approach was not associated with DFS or OS. In conclusion, single-port thoracoscopic lobectomy was associated with reduced surgical trauma, decreased postoperative pain and inflammation, and improved pulmonary function recovery, without compromising lymph node dissection, short-term safety, or 3-year oncological outcomes. These findings support the continued use and wider adoption of single-port VATS in appropriately selected patients with NSCLC, while acknowledging that Stage I disease predominance limits generalizability to more advanced stages.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose To assess pulmonary gas exchange in participants with cystic fibrosis (CF) relative to control participants, evaluate the effect of CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy, and assess subclinical lung disease using xenon 129 (129Xe) MRI. Materials and Methods Participants with CF and control participants were prospectively enrolled between October 2019 and February 2024 and underwent 129Xe MRI and spirometry. Images from gaseous xenon, xenon dissolved in pulmonary capillary red blood cells (RBCs), and dissolved in the gas-exchange membrane (interstitial tissue and capillary plasma) were binned into three compartments to generate maps of ventilation, RBC transfer, and membrane uptake. Spirometric and imaging differences between participants with CF and control participants were assessed using analysis of variance with Tukey post hoc corrections, and associations were analyzed using Kendall rank correlation. Results Sixty-one participants with CF (median age, 14.2 years; IQR, 10.0-19.7 years; 33 female) and 47 controls (median age, 24.9 years; IQR, 20.9-29.2 years; 25 males) were included. For participants with CF, spirometry (percent predicted) was normal: forced expiratory volume after 1 second (median, 98.2%; IQR, 87.2%-109%), forced vital capacity (median, 104%; IQR, 96.8%-112%), and forced expiratory flow between 25% and 75% forced vital capacity (median, 88.1%; IQR, 69.9%-108%). Participants with CF had a higher ventilation defect percentage (2.50% vs 1.40%; P < .001), RBC transfer (0.00354 vs 0.00325; P = .0104), and membrane uptake (0.0096 vs 0.0076; P < .001) than controls. Membrane uptake correlated with elevated RBC transfer (τ = 0.62; P < .001) for participants with CF on and off CFTR modulator therapy. Conclusion Participants with CF had higher RBC transfer and membrane uptake than control participants. Membrane uptake was elevated in participants with CF exhibiting normal spirometry and receiving highly effective CFTR modulator therapy. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To compare low-attenuation analysis (LAA) with visual scoring and explore their application in the detection of emphysema in low-dose CT (LDCT) scans. METHODS: A random cohort of 352 CT examinations from health-check participants was selected from a lung cancer screening(LCS) dataset. Scans were evaluated for emphysema by four readers according to latest Fleischner criteria, and emphysema was quantified by LAA with thresholds from -900 HU to -980 HU. Fleiss' Kappa assessed inter-reader agreement on visual detection and severity classification. Cases with full agreement on emphysema presence were used to compare LAA quantification and visual detection. Spearman correlation test measured their correlation and Cohen's Kappa evaluated the agreement between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection. RESULTS: Agreement among four observers was found in 266 cases on emphysema presence based on visual evaluation (K = 0.738, 0.737-0.739). Concordance between emphysema presence using a LAA% cutoff of 6% and binary visual classification was 61.3% (163/266, Cohen's Kappa:0.173. Spearman analysis showed a correlation between LAA% and visual scores (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: LAA emphysema quantification shows in comparison with visual scoring limited performance for discrimination of normal and emphysematous lung parenchyma in a Low dose CT Lung cancer screening dataset. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Full agreement among four readers regarding visual emphysema classification was achieved in only three-quarters of cases. Limited concordance was found between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

papers.abstract_en: Although multi-hit TP53 mutations correlate with rapid disease progression, treatment resistance, recurrence, and poor survival, their occurrence within an individual TP53 gene molecule (cbTP53) remains unexplored. Consequently, the impact of cbTP53 on protein conformation, transcriptional architecture, and oncogenicity is unknown. We show that cbTP53 with combined mutations (Y220C+R248Q+R282Q) does not drastically alter local stability or structural conformation, but significantly affects TP53 binding to DNA promoters comparing it to a single Y220C mutation. Functionally, cbTP53 promotes divergent cellular phenotypes, characterized by enhanced cell proliferation, increased formation of multicellular tumor spheroids (MCTS) and spheroids, altered responses to chemotherapeutic drugs (e.g., cisplatin, carboplatin) and p53 inhibitors (e.g., MB710, PK11007), and increased resistance to carboplatin-induced DNA damage. Furthermore, cbTP53 is linked to distinct immune cell profiles (e.g., CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, nature killer cells, dendritic cells), more circulating tumor cells, a higher rate of tumor engraftment, and an increased number of lung tumor nodules. Mechanistically, introduction of R248Q/R282Q mutations changes 42.7% of Y220C-regulated gene expression, and cbTP53 (vs Y220C) owns a distinctive transcriptomic signature with 1,004 up- and 1,747 down-regulated genes. cbTP53 shows the enhanced binding affinity in the promoters of inflammatory cytokines, leading to their increased production. This study establishes causative and mechanistic links of cbTP53 to lung aggressive cancer metastasis and disease progression, providing a novel perspective on the genetics of TP53 mutations in cancer.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to estimate the incidence, mortality, and overall survival (OS) of esophageal cancer (EC) and to evaluate the association of clinicopathological characteristics and treatment modality with OS. METHODS: A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted using data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) in rural central India. The dataset included 545 incident EC cases registered between 2010 and 2019, of which 476 were eligible for OS analysis. Incidence and mortality rates were estimated, OS was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify prognostic factors. Prespecified sensitivity analyses, including metastasis-adjusted and age-stratified Cox regression models, were performed to assess the robustness of the primary multivariable findings. RESULTS: The age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) of overall EC cases was 3.99 per 100,000 population (95% CI: 3.50-4.47), while the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR) was 3.29 per 100,000 population (95% CI: 2.94-3.64). The overall median survival was 178.33 days (95% CI: 115.49-234.48). The OS rates at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years were 31.3%, 19.7%, 17.4%, and 14.6%, respectively. OS differed significantly according to tumor site (χ² = 5.24, p = 0.043), treatment modality (χ² = 15.42, p = 0.031), and metastatic status (χ² = 162.64, p < 0.001) on Kaplan-Meier analysis. Median survival was 232 days (95% CI: 159.59-304.41) for localized disease, 199 days (95% CI: 166.38-231.61) for regional disease, 68 days (95% CI: 54.21-81.79) for distant disease, and 28 days (95% CI: 15.56-40.44) for advanced disease. On univariable Cox regression, patients with middle-third tumors had a lower hazard of death than those with upper-third tumors (HR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.56-0.98; p = 0.036), and this remained significant after adjustment for metastatic status and in the age-stratified sensitivity model, while metastatic disease was associated with progressively higher mortality. Radiotherapy plus chemotherapy and surgery plus chemotherapy were independently associated with lower mortality after multivariable adjustment (HR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.28-0.85, p = 0.011; HR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.21-0.94, p = 0.035, respectively). Age, sex, and histological type were not significantly associated with OS. CONCLUSION: EC demonstrated a substantial mortality burden and poor OS in this population-based cohort. Metastatic status was the strongest associated prognostic factor, while tumor site and treatment modality were associated with survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis. Radiotherapy plus chemotherapy and surgery plus chemotherapy remained independently associated with lower mortality after multivariable adjustment. These findings highlight the importance of early diagnosis, accurate assessment of disease extent, and appropriate multimodal management of EC.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pleural effusion remains diagnostically challenging when standard thoracentesis does not establish an aetiology. This pilot analysis described sequential biomarker measurements in patients proceeding to medical thoracoscopy and explored their associations and discrimination across final diagnostic classifications. METHODS: Prospectively collected data from a single-centre tertiary referral cohort were analysed. Pleural-fluid adenosine deaminase (ADA) and serum complement components 3 and 4 (C3 and C4) were obtained on day 1, whereas pleural-fluid cancer antigen 125 (CA125) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) were obtained at the day 7/thoracoscopy evaluation. Final classifications were based on a composite reference standard integrating thoracoscopy, histopathology, microbiology, cytology, imaging, and clinical follow-up. Analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: Amongst 75 patients, 6 (8.0%) were classified as tuberculous pleural effusion (TB-PE), 33 (44.0%) as malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and 36 (48.0%) as other non-tuberculous, non-malignant pleural effusions. ADA differed across groups (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.002; Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.010) and showed exploratory discrimination for TB-PE (area under the curve [AUC] 0.934; bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.855-0.995). At the conventional ≥ 40 U/L threshold, sensitivity was 83.3%, specificity 93.4%, positive predictive value (PPV) 55.6%, negative predictive value (NPV) 98.3%, positive likelihood ratio (LR+) 12.7, and negative likelihood ratio (LR-) 0.18. CA125, LDH, C3 and C4 did not show significant omnibus group differences after reanalysis. In a post hoc sensitivity analysis excluding 26 patients retained as non-specific pleuritis (n = 49), ADA remained significantly different across groups (P = 0.004; q = 0.022). CONCLUSIONS: In this selected thoracoscopy cohort, day 1 pleural-fluid ADA showed the clearest exploratory signal, including after exclusion of non-specific pleuritis, but estimates were based on only six TB-PE cases and do not establish stand-alone utility or a role in avoiding thoracoscopy. The remaining biomarkers showed no robust aetiology-specific signal. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06159179.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, including among patients diagnosed with potentially curable disease. Current decisions regarding perioperative treatment and follow-up rely on a limited number of established prognostic factors. Further knowledge is needed regarding the clinical, histopathological, and molecular factors associated with subsequent metastatic disease, particularly brain metastasis (BM), which is associated with poor prognosis. We investigated these factors in a large cohort of patients with surgically resected stage I-III lung cancer followed for more than five years. BM was associated with higher pathological tumour and lymph-node stage and younger age at surgery. Lung adenocarcinoma was associated with a higher risk of BM than lung squamous cell carcinoma. Several molecular alterations were associated with metastatic disease or BM, including KRAS mutations in lung adenocarcinoma and NFE2L2 mutations in lung squamous cell carcinoma. Additional associations involving specific EGFR and KRAS mutation subtypes and rarer alterations were observed, but were based on small numbers of cases and should be considered exploratory. Several of the associated genes are involved in the RAS/MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, or NRF2-related pathways. However, pathway activation and causality could not be established in this observational study. These findings support further investigation of clinical, histopathological, and molecular factors associated with metastatic progression after surgical resection. Validation in larger, independent, stage-stratified and contemporary cohorts with comprehensive treatment data is required before the identified molecular alterations can be considered for clinical risk stratification or surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: The 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting presented substantial new data on antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in lung cancer, highlighting the ongoing expansion of ADC-based strategies from later-line treatment toward first-line combination regimens. This focused narrative review summarizes and discusses the efficacy and safety findings of ADCs targeting TROP2, HER2, Nectin-4, PD-L1, c-Met, B7-H3, DLL3, SEZ6, and other emerging targets in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with particular attention to emerging ADC plus immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations in the first-line setting. Taken together, these findings highlight an expanding ADC landscape in lung cancer. However, many of the emerging strategies remain supported primarily by preliminary conference-reported or early-phase data and therefore require confirmation in mature peer-reviewed studies and adequately powered randomized clinical trials.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a major subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality despite major therapeutic advances. Precision oncology has revolutionized the management of LUAD by identifying actionable molecular biomarkers and developing targeted therapies. In this review, we summarize the major predictive biomarkers in LUAD, including EGFR, KRAS, ALK, ROS1, MET, RET, BRAF, HER2, NTRK, and PD-L1, and describe the currently approved targeted therapies and emerging therapeutic strategies. Recent advances in selective inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, and immune checkpoint inhibitors that have improved clinical outcomes in molecularly defined patient populations are highlighted. The review also discusses the molecular basis of acquired resistance, such as on-target mutations, bypass signalling activation, histological transformation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition that continue to limit long-term therapeutic efficacy. We also discuss emerging strategies to overcome resistance, including combination therapies, next-generation inhibitors, liquid biopsy-guided monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted precision medicine. Collectively, these findings highlight the need for comprehensive molecular characterization and integrated biomarker-guided treatment strategies to improve therapeutic decision-making and clinical outcomes in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Approximately 2% of lung tumours are pulmonary carcinoids (PCs), divided into typical (90%) and atypical (AC) (10%). The link with external exposure to carcinogens remains controversial. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between occupational exposure to carcinogens and PC tumours. METHODS: A PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review was performed. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed and Embase (January 2025). Studies were reviewed, data extracted, analysed and summarised narratively. RESULTS: 1302 studies were reviewed. 27 original studies and seven conference papers on topics including exposure to cigarette smoke (n=23) and asbestos (n=6), or mechanistic information, were included. Following the collapse of the World Trade Center in 2001, carcinoids accounted for 6% of lung cancer cases in people exposed to the resulting dust (9% in women, 3% in men). The proportion of ACs among carcinoids rose from 9.3% (controls) to 16.3% (smokers) and from ∼25% to 45% (probable versus definite asbestos exposure). Basic research has identified biological pathways linking harmful exposures (such as asbestos and cigarette smoke) to neuroendocrine cell proliferation and the potential progression of PCs to higher-grade lung tumours. DISCUSSION: The significance these of findings is limited due to 1) the limited number of studies, 2) the small number of tumours within those studies and 3) the lack of rigid diagnostic (morphological and molecular) criteria for PCs in most studies. Nevertheless, a consistent finding is a higher proportion of AC among carcinoids, particularly following asbestos exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Based on these findings, a link between carcinogenic substances (especially asbestos and cigarette smoke) and carcinoids seems plausible. More stringent analyses in epidemiological surveys are needed to further clarify the pathogenesis of PCs.

papers.abstract_en: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutant-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) frequently develops acquired resistance to third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), particularly through the EGFR C797S mutation. Existing EGFR-targeting proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) remain limited by unfavorable pharmacokinetics and suboptimal selectivity inherited from their parent TKIs. To address these limitations, we developed HQY1480, a next-generation PROTAC derived from the macrocyclic fourth-generation EGFR inhibitor BI-4020. Systematic linker and E3 ligase ligand optimization enabled potent and selective degradation of multiple clinically relevant EGFR mutants with single-digit nanomolar DC50 values. HQY1480 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics, stronger suppression of oncogenic signaling than BI-4020, and no detectable off-target degradation in proteomic profiling. In xenograft models, HQY1480 outperformed BI-4020, overcame osimertinib resistance, and effectively inhibited tumor growth at low doses, while inducing robust EGFR degradation in patient-derived xenografts. These findings establish HQY1480 as an effective and well-tolerated lead PROTAC for EGFR-mutant NSCLC with acquired resistance to third-generation TKIs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema-associated pulmonary hypertension (CPFE-PH) has emerged as a distinct third category of PH, yet its detailed clinical-hemodynamic profile, pathological features, and comparative outcomes remain poorly defined. This study aims to characterize the phenotype of CPFE-PH and compare it with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease-related PH (COPD-PH) and idiopathic interstitial pneumonia-related PH (IIP-PH). METHODS: In this multicenter cohort study, we analyzed 113 patients with CPFE-PH, 277 with COPD-PH, and 78 with IIP-PH, all diagnosed by right heart catheterization. Clinical, physiological, imaging, pathological, treatment response, and survival data were statistically compared across groups. RESULTS: CPFE-PH patients were older, predominantly male smokers, and exhibited preserved ventilatory function but severely reduced diffusing capacity (DLCO 31.6% predicted, IQR 24.8-37.8). They had the most severe hemodynamic compromise (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 41 mmHg, pulmonary vascular resistance 7.4 Wood units), a high prevalence of mediastinal lymphadenopathy (81.4%), and universal capillary hemangiomatosis-like remodeling, a pathological feature absent in COPD-PH and rarely observed in IIP-PH. Pulmonary arterial hypertension-targeted therapy failed to improve functional or biomarker outcomes, and transplant-free survival was shortest in CPFE-PH (median 32 months) compared with COPD-PH and IIP-PH (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: CPFE-PH appears to represent a severe phenotype within Group 3 PH, in which prominent capillary remodeling, including hemangiomatosis-like changes, may contribute to its clinical, radiological, and functional manifestations, distinguish it from other Group 3 PH types. CLINICAL TRIAL: Chinese Clinical Study.org, No: ChiCTR2000032212, Registration Date: 2020-04-23; URL: http://www.chictr.org.cn/ .

papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram based on clinical and computed tomography (CT) features for the preoperative prediction of invasiveness in patients with solitary pulmonary ground-glass nodules (GGNs). We retrospectively analyzed 846 patients with solitary GGNs who underwent surgical resection at the Lung Cancer Center of West China Hospital between November 2022 and January 2024. All nodules were pathologically confirmed as atypical adenomatous hyperplasia (AAH), adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS), minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (MIA), or invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC). Patients were classified into a non-invasive group (including AAH, AIS, and MIA) and an IAC group based on postoperative pathological results. Clinical data and CT features before surgery were collected. Patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 592) and a validation cohort (n = 254) in a ratio of 7:3. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, followed by multivariate logistic regression to identify independent predictors and construct a nomogram model. The variance inflation factor (VIF) was used to evaluate multicollinearity among the candidate predictors. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that the maximum tumor diameter (OR = 39.82, 95% CI: 16.29-97.32), consolidation-to-tumor ratio (0.5<CTR<1, OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.36-4.63), vacuole sign (OR = 2.29, 95% CI: 1.29-4.07), pleura traction sign (OR = 3.03, 95% CI: 1.66-5.53), and the presence of solid component on the mediastinal window (OR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.46-7.28) were independent risk factors for IAC. The nomogram constructed based on these variables demonstrated good discriminative ability, with AUC values of 0.930 and 0.913 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between the predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA indicated favorable clinical utility. Consequently, this nomogram based on the maximum tumor diameter, CTR, vacuole sign, pleura traction sign, and the presence of solid component on the mediastinal window, provides an effective and noninvasive tool for preoperative prediction of the invasiveness of solitary GGNs.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: To summarize the clinical features, treatment patterns and survival outcomes of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) combined with connective tissue disease (CTD), and to determine whether CTD independently influences prognosis and treatment-related toxicity in this special patient population. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we enrolled 200 consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed NSCLC. Among them, 95 patients met the diagnostic criteria for CTD were set as the CTD group, and the remaining 105 patients with simple NSCLC as the control group. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), baseline tumor characteristics, metastatic patterns, first-line treatment patterns and delivery, and treatment-related adverse events (AEs). We adopted Kaplan-Meier method for survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression model for prognostic analysis. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the prognostic effect of CTD and identify independent survival predictors. RESULTS: The CTD group presented more severe intrathoracic tumor dissemination, including higher incidence of bilateral pulmonary lesions (P = 0.042) and pleural effusion (P = 0.011). Compared with controls, the CTD group were less likely to receive platinum-based doublet chemotherapy (P = 0.035), cisplatin-based chemotherapy (P = 0.017), immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-containing therapy (P = 0.009) and thoracic radiotherapy (P = 0.029). Meanwhile, the CTD group had higher risks of chemotherapy dose reduction (P = 0.011), treatment delay longer than 7 days (P = 0.015) and early treatment discontinuation (P = 0.002). In survival outcomes, the median PFS was 5.4 vs 7.8 months (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.17-2.13; P = 0.003), and the median OS was 9.7 vs 14.6 months (HR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.29-2.40; P<0.001). The incidence of grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs was significantly higher in the CTD group (P = 0.010). Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that CTD was an independent adverse prognostic factor for poor OS (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.01-1.97; P = 0.044). CONCLUSION: For patients diagnosed with NSCLC, comorbid CTD is correlated with aggravated intrathoracic tumor dissemination, reduced treatment intensity and treatment tolerance, increased severe toxicity, and dismal long-term survival.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: ORCHARD (NCT03944772) was a biomarker-directed, phase II, platform study conducted to characterize resistance mechanisms and evaluate novel treatment combinations in patients with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following progression on first-line osimertinib. We report results from the module evaluating osimertinib plus platinum-based chemotherapy. METHODS: Patients received osimertinib (80 mg once daily) plus ≤ 4 cycles of platinum-based doublet chemotherapy (pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin AUC5) on day 1 of every 21-day cycle, followed by pemetrexed maintenance until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or another discontinuation criterion. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1. Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), duration of response (DoR), overall survival (OS), and safety. RESULTS: Thirty-one patients received study treatment. Eight patients had a confirmed partial response (ORR 26%; 80% CI, 16-39). Median DoR was 7.6 months (95% CI, 4.2-not calculable). Median PFS was 5.6 months (95% CI, 4.0-7.5); PFS events were reported in 29 (94%) patients. Median OS was 10.9 months (95% CI, 8.5-15.0); 20 (65%) patients had died at data cut-off. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 20 (65%) patients; AEs leading to discontinuation of any treatment occurred in 7 (23%) patients. CONCLUSION: In patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC who had progressed on first-line osimertinib, osimertinib plus platinum-based chemotherapy demonstrated a modest clinical benefit and manageable safety profile, consistent with the individual drug profiles.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Virtual-assisted lung mapping (VAL-MAP) is a safe and useful procedure for identifying suitable lines for sublobar lung resections. Nonetheless, the current VAL-MAP technique using a thin bronchoscope limits access to peripheral lung regions, including the upper lobes or the S6 region. METHODS: To overcome this limitation, we developed a new technique utilizing an ultrathin bronchoscope (UTB), termed 'UTB VAL-MAP', enabling precise dye marking of the visceral pleura which is difficult to access with a thin bronchoscope. We retrospectively evaluated the efficacy and safety of UTB VAL-MAP with those of conventional VAL-MAP at our institution. RESULTS: Overall, 178 preoperative markings (75 patients) were included: 74 markings in 35 patients in the UTB VAL-MAP group and 104 markings in 40 patients in the conventional VAL-MAP group. The overall detection rate in the UTB VAL-MAP group was significantly higher than that in the conventional VAL-MAP group [97.3% (72/74) vs. 84.6% (88/104); P = 0.005]. Furthermore, the marking success rate using indigo carmine in the UTB VAL-MAP group was higher for lesions located in the upper lobe and S6 region than that in the conventional VAL-MAP group (P < 0.001). In multivariate generalized estimating equations models, UTB use (odds ratio = 7.390, P = 0.015) was significantly associated with overall detection rate. No severe procedure-related complications occurred in either group. CONCLUSION: UTB VAL-MAP appears useful for increasing the rate of successful visceral pleura marking, particularly in the upper lobes or S6 areas, which the conventional VAL-MAP technique has difficulty reaching, without increasing complications.

Methods Adult hospitalizations not coded as elective, with a primary diagnosis of COPD exacerbation and tracheostomy, in the U.S. National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022) were classified as OST or PDT using ICD-10-PCS approach codes. Utilization trends, in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), and inflation-adjusted charges were compared using survey-weighted multivariable models and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), with further adjustment for timing, coded severity, and pandemic period. Results Of an estimated 2,970 hospitalizations (594 sampled), 36.5% involved PDT. Annual volumes declined for PDT (215 to 115; P-trend=0.023) and OST (480 to 165; P-trend=0.003). In-hospital mortality was 13.5% (PDT 14.3% vs OST 13.0%; P=0.662). Mortality was higher in 2020-2022 than in 2016-2019 among OST hospitalizations (21.3% vs 10.2%; P=0.006) but not among PDT hospitalizations (18.3% vs 12.7%; P=0.29); annual trends did not differ significantly between approaches (P for interaction=0.061). After adjustment, PDT was not associated with mortality (RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.68-1.66), LOS (-0.63 days; 95% CI, -4.19 to 2.94), or charges (ratio, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.85-1.12); estimates were consistent with IPTW, timing and severity adjustment, exclusion of 2020, and within both periods. Conclusions Both OST and PDT volumes declined. No significant association was detected between approach and short-term outcomes, although estimates were imprecise. The mortality increase within OST hospitalizations, concentrated in the pandemic period, warrants cautious interpretation given potential changes in case mix, treatment selection, pandemic-related practice, and unmeasured severity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: De novo malignancies are a major cause of late death following lung transplantation (LTx). Although previous reports from Japan have identified post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) as the most common de novo malignancy, comprehensive long-term data on the spectrum, treatment, and outcomes of de novo malignancies remain limited. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of 413 patients who underwent LTx at our institution between April 2002 and December 2025 and analyzed the incidence, characteristics, and outcomes of de novo malignancies. RESULTS: De novo malignancy was diagnosed in 53 patients (12.8%), comprising 18 cases of PTLD and 37 cases of solid tumors (42 tumors in total). The cumulative incidence of PTLD was 3.1% at 1 year and remained stable thereafter, whereas the incidence of solid tumors increased steadily over time, reaching 16.8% at 10 years after LTx. PTLD and solid tumors showed distinct temporal patterns, with median times to onset of 8.0 months and 64.0 months, respectively. Regarding post-LTx lung cancer, five of the six cases (83.3%) originated in the native lung after single LTx. The 2-year overall survival after malignancy diagnosis was significantly higher in the curative treatment group than in the non-curative group (87.9% vs. 16.7%, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that the risk of solid malignancies continues to increase during long-term follow-up after LTx. The favorable outcomes observed among patients receiving curative treatment are considered to reflect earlier detection and better baseline patients' condition, underscoring the importance of post-transplant cancer surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: In September 2021, the eruption of the Tajogaite volcano on La Palma (Spain) released large amounts of toxic gases and particulate matter over three months. This study, part of the ASHES Project, analyses the serum cytokine profile and its relationship with exposure to these pollutants in general population, asthma patients, and occupationally exposed workers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 102 participants (69 women; median age 50 years) were included. Structured interviews were conducted, and serum samples were collected to quantify 48 biomarkers related to TH1, TH2, and TH17 inflammatory responses (Olink®). Participants were classified into three groups: healthy population (n = 66), occupationally exposed workers (n = 13), and asthmatic patients (n = 23). Comparisons were performed between healthy population vs. asthmatics and healthy population vs. occupational group. RESULTS: Occupationally exposed workers showed the highest exposure (median 10 h), compared with 6 h in the healthy population and 5 h in asthmatics (p = 0.006). This group, with highest exposure, had increased levels of IL-2, IL-7, IL-17A, and IL-17F compared with the general population. Asthmatic patients showed higher levels of IL-2, IL-7, TNFSF12, CXCL10, IL-17C, CCL3, and CCL4, and lower levels of IL-15 and MMP12 (p < 0.05). A strong positive correlation between IL-4 and exposure time (r = 0.7935, p < 0.0001), and negative correlations with CCL8, CXCL11, and TNF-α were observed in asthmatics. CONCLUSIONS: Volcanic emissions are associated with exposure- and disease-dependent immune responses. Asthmatics show heightened TH1/TH2/TH17 activation, while highly exposed workers display a TH17-skewed profile, with the general population maintaining a balanced response, suggesting greater vulnerability in asthma patients.

papers.abstract_en: Metastasis represents a major cause of chemotherapy failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). To explore the role of CYP1B1 enzymatic activity in NSCLC metastasis, we established A549 and H460 cells overexpressing wild-type CYP1B1, an activity-enhanced variant (L432V), and an activity-reduced variant (N203S). CYP1B1 did not affect cell proliferation but promoted migration and invasion, with the extent of these effects being associated with CYP1B1 enzymatic activity. We then designed and synthesized a series of CYP1B1 inhibitors. Compound G26 exhibited high selectivity over other CYP isoforms (IC50 = 5.33 nM), showed favorable microsomal metabolic stability with species differences, significantly inhibited migration and invasion in A549 and H460 cells, exhibited moderate oral bioavailability in SD rats (F = 20.7%), and showed a favorable safety profile in mice.
