papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of "Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis". IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107-1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibility (relative standard deviation, RSD = 9.1%). Analysis of clinical serum samples revealed significantly elevated EV-PD-L1 levels in patients with lung cancer compared with healthy donors and patients with benign nodule (p < 0.01). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yielded areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.849 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from healthy donors and 0.860 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from patients with benign nodules, which are superior to those of the conventional serum biomarkers CEA and Cyfra21-1. By addressing the cost, complexity, and slow response of current methods, IMAN offers a simple, cost-effective platform for direct EV surface protein detection without complex instrumentation, providing a novel tool for the noninvasive lung cancer diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: Erlotinib hydrochloride (ERL), an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in non-small cell lung cancer, is a classic example of drug polymorphism. However, the influence of crystallisation methods, PLGA, and thermal ageing on its polymorphic behaviour remains unexplored. This study investigated ERL polymorphism in binary mixtures prepared by blending, co-grinding, and solvent evaporation. PXRD revealed that blending and co-grinding retained ERL polymorphic form A, whereas solvent evaporation yielded form B in all binary mixtures. Thermal ageing has a significant effect on ERL crystallinity. DSC melting endotherms for form A are at 213.75 and 233.26°C, whereas form B shows a single melting endotherm at 231.96°C. MDSC efficiently captured the melt-mediated recrystallisation of form A. Further, ATR-FTIR with chemometric analysis differentiated the polymorphs into form A (anti) and form B (syn) conformations based on spectral regions at 3270 cm⁻1 (non-classical H-bonding) and 2540 cm⁻1 (N⁺-H···Cl⁻ interactions). SEM revealed plate-like and needle-like morphologies for forms A and B, respectively. Conversely, saturation solubility results reported higher solubility for the solvent-evaporated drug, due to its crystal morphology. Drug content by RP-HPLC (98-102% w/w) confirmed that the observed changes were solely physical transitions. Overall, this study provides insights into the development of ERL-loaded PLGA microspheres.

papers.abstract_en: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), a major subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, presents substantial therapeutic challenges due to limited targeted therapy options and prevalent drug resistance. In this study, we characterised 1-octen-3-ol, an active compound derived from bamboo leaves, as a bioactive natural compound with anti-LUSC activity. In vitro, 1-octen-3-ol significantly suppressed LUSC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis. Network pharmacology predicted the PI3K/AKT pathway as a central mediator of its activity. Mechanistic studies confirmed that 1-octen-3-ol inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, accompanied by increased expression of p53 and cleaved-caspase3. The PI3K agonist 740Y-P and AKT agonist SC79 partially reversed the effects of 1-octen-3-ol on LUSC cell migration, invasion, colony formation, and protein expression, underscoring the critical role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. In vivo, 1-octen-3-ol markedly suppressed LUSC xenograft growth, and its tumor-suppressive effect was abrogated by co-administration of either the PI3K or AKT agonist. This study is the first to demonstrate that 1-octen-3-ol exerts potent inhibition of LUSC progression via modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, thereby activating p53 and initiating caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the anti-LUSC activity of 1-octen-3-ol, a natural volatile small-molecule, and support further lead-discovery efforts based on natural-product sources.

papers.abstract_en: Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) agonists hold great promise for cancer immunotherapy. Our previously identified TLR2 agonist SMU-Z1 contains a nitro group associated with potential metabolic toxicity. Herein, 47 analogs were designed and synthesized to mitigate toxicity, and SMU-H1 emerged as a potent, selective TLR2 agonist (EC50 = 5.14 ± 0.7 nM) with superior safety relative to SMU-Z1. papers.abstract_en: Accurate discrimination of lung cancer subtypes and evaluation of chemotherapeutic efficacy remain critical challenges in precision oncology owing to the heterogeneity of tumor cellular microenvironments. Herein, we report a mitochondrial microenvironment-responsive fluorescence sensor array, MR-SA, for intelligent analysis of lung cancer cells and chemotherapeutic efficacy. Four mitochondria-targeting fluorescent probes were rationally designed by integrating indolium salts with environment-sensitive fluorophores, enabling selective sensing of mitochondrial hypoxia, polarity, pH, and viscosity in living cells. Benefiting from distinct cross-reactive fluorescence response patterns and broad emission coverage ranging from 573 to 734 nm, MR-SA generated multidimensional fluorescence fingerprints for different lung cancer subtypes while minimizing spectral crosstalk. The chemotherapy-induced mitochondrial alterations were monitored using MR-SA and combined with outlier analysis for evaluation of chemotherapeutic efficacy and drug resistance in nonsmall cell lung cancer cells. Furthermore, MR-SA fluorescence images were integrated with ResNet, a deep-learning framework, enabling rapid and accurate blind classification of lung cancer cells with a recognition accuracy of 99.71%. Thus, MR-SA successfully distinguished lung adenocarcinoma, lung squamous cell carcinoma, large cell carcinoma, and small cell lung cancer cells through differential mitochondrial microenvironment profiling. This work establishes a versatile fluorescence sensing strategy for multidimensional mitochondrial analysis and provides a promising analytical platform for intelligent cancer cell profiling and chemotherapeutic evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: In cancer diagnosis, liquid biopsy is a minimally invasive method, yet its diagnostic performance is constrained by insufficient sensitivity and restricted blood biomarkers. Therefore, the use of additional invasive methods is unavoidable to identify cancer-specific information, such as subtypes, stages, and mutation status. Here, we propose a deep-learning-based method for differential diagnosis, in which group-specific feature importance is assigned to Raman spectra of extracellular vesicles (EVs) and the spectra are decoded. The feature importance was extracted from the training dataset using explainable AI (XAI) to emphasize key spectral patterns. These features were then applied to the original spectra as weights to develop an AI-based diagnostic algorithm. As a result, the algorithm successfully identified the presence of lung cancer, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.98. Moreover, it demonstrated the capability of precision cancer diagnosis with an average AUC of 0.96 across the detailed cancer information. These preliminary findings suggest the potential of liquid-biopsy-based differential diagnosis and its possible contribution to the establishment of rapid and tailored treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Cigarette smoking is a primary etiological factor in lung cancer, and 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone (NNK) is a prototypical tobacco-specific nitrosamine carcinogen. Although FTO has been implicated in the progression of various cancers, its specific role in smoking-associated lung carcinogenesis remains incompletely understood. In this study, we built a model of NNK-induced malignant transformation of human bronchial epithelial Beas-2B cells (designated Beas-2B-NNK cells) to explore the function and regulatory mechanism of FTO during NNK-induced lung carcinogenesis. Through quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) assays, FTO levels were found to be notably higher in Beas-2B-NNK cells when compared with their parental Beas-2B cell line. Then, knocking down FTO expression using short hairpin RNA (shRNA) led to marked repression of proliferation, migration, and cell-cycle progression in Beas-2B-NNK cells. Bioinformatics analysis revealed a positive correlation between FTO and DIXDC1, and when FTO was knocked out, the sharpest drop in DIXDC1 expression was seen in Beas-2B-NNK cells. Combined bioinformatic and Western blot analysis observed that DIXDC1 regulates the malignant transformation of Beas-2B-NNK cells via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. In summary, these findings suggest that FTO participates in NNK-induced malignant transformation of Beas-2B cells via the DIXDC1/PI3K/AKT signaling axis.

papers.abstract_en: Exhaled breath analysis offers a noninvasive route for disease screening, yet its practical implementation is constrained by ultratrace analyte levels, high humidity, and limited selectivity of existing enrichment materials. Herein, we report the rational design of a carboxyl-functionalized hyper-cross-linked polymer (HCPs-COOH) as a high-performance solid-phase microextraction (SPME) coating and its integration into a two-step preconcentration workflow for breath analysis. The HCPs-COOH exhibits an ultrahigh specific surface area (1916 m2 g-1) and hierarchical micromesoporosity, enabling high-capacity uptake and rapid mass transfer. Surface carboxyl (-COOH) groups introduce specific interactions (hydrogen bonding and dipole-dipole), while the hydrophobic framework mitigates water interference, collectively enhancing affinity and selectivity toward diverse volatile organic compounds (VOCs) classes. Coupling Tenax-TA adsorption tube sampling with solvent elution and headspace HCPs-COOH-SPME, followed by GC-MS detection, affords a sensitive and robust method for the simultaneous determination of five lung cancer-related biomarkers. The method achieved limits of quantification of 0.10-0.21 pg mL-1, excellent precision, and high enrichment factors up to 5304. Compared with commercial fibers and reported approaches, the HCPs-COOH coating provides faster equilibration, higher enrichment efficiency, and improved tolerance to humid matrices. Application to exhaled breath samples from lung cancer patients and healthy volunteers reveals consistently elevated levels of all five biomarkers in the patient group, demonstrating clear discriminative capability. This work establishes a versatile, cost-effective platform that integrates high-capacity adsorption with selective SPME enrichment, providing a powerful strategy for ultrasensitive breathomics and advancing the clinical translation of noninvasive cancer screening.

papers.abstract_en: Intratumoral injection of cisplatin into lung cancer is feasible and can increase local drug exposure while reducing systemic toxicity. However, its success relies on achieving sufficient drug exposure to the tumor, which has not been quantitatively evaluated in a clinical setting. In the context of a Phase I clinical trial of intratumoral cisplatin injections into resectable lung tumors via robotic bronchoscopy (N = 6), we developed a quantitative framework to assess delivery effectiveness and long-term cisplatin exposure in tumors. Initial injectate retention was estimated using a novel image analytics pipeline based on intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography scans, by assuming that emerging high-attenuation regions are due to injectate deposition. Long-term drug exposure was estimated using a novel pharmacokinetic model tailored for intratumoral drug delivery and informed by sequential venous blood draws following the injections. The area under the platinum concentration curve in the tumor compartment at t = 3-21 h and platinum concentration in the tumor compartment (t = 3-6 h), estimated from the fitted pharmacokinetic model, showed a strong monotonic association with percentage pathological necrosis assessed post-resection by three independent, blinded pathologists (Spearman's ρ = 0.93, 95% bootstrap CI 0.67-1.00, unadjusted exact p = 0.033), which was not statistically significant when corrected for multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.17). No other pharmacokinetic variable correlated was significantly correlated with necrosis or other pathological response metrics prior to multiple comparison correction. This result aligns with the known time-concentration dependency of cisplatin action in tumor. Further studies will be needed to evaluate this observation for repeatability and clinical relevance. Our approach provides a framework for estimating intratumoral drug exposure in clinical settings, which may help with the interpretation of clinical trial outcomes and future evaluation of injection strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perioperative regurgitation of gastric or esophageal contents remains a severe complication during anesthesia. While standard fasting protocols and rapid sequence induction (RSI) are routinely employed, esophageal dilatation creates a hidden reservoir for retained food and secretions that conventional methods often fail to mitigate. Furthermore, standard gastric ultrasound lacks the field of view to detect mid-to-proximal esophageal pooling. CASE PRESENTATION: We present two parallel cases emphasizing this critical challenge. Case 1 involves a 68-year-old male with esophageal carcinoma who experienced massive regurgitation of white foam during RSI, despite five days of preoperative fasting. Airway security was ultimately achieved after intensified suctioning. Case 2 describes a 42-year-old female with achalasia and marked esophageal dilatation. Informed by preoperative computed tomography (CT) and barium swallow imaging, she was safely managed using targeted pre-anesthetic conscious endoscopic suctioning, leading to an uneventful induction and peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM). CONCLUSION: These cases highlight the limitations of conventional fasting in managing proximal pooling. They underscore the diagnostic value of preoperative cross-sectional imaging, such as CT, when clinically indicated. Active pre-induction decompression, specifically through tailored endoscopic evacuation, is a valuable adjunctive strategy for preventing perioperative regurgitation in selected patients with megaesophagus.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative esophageal achalasia after lung surgery is extremely rare. Vagal nerve injury has been proposed as a possible mechanism of postsurgical esophageal dysmotility. We report a rare case of esophageal achalasia following robot-assisted lung cancer surgery. CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old woman with lung adenocarcinoma (cT1cN0M0, stage IA3) underwent robot-assisted left lower lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection. On postoperative day 2, she developed vomiting and difficulty eating. Computed tomography revealed esophageal dilatation with retained food, and esophagography demonstrated absent esophageal peristalsis, narrowing at the esophagogastric junction, and contrast retention. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed no mechanical obstruction. High-resolution manometry confirmed esophageal achalasia. Pneumatic dilation was performed on postoperative day 15, resulting in improvement of esophagogastric junction relaxation. She was discharged on postoperative day 24 and remained well without recurrence of achalasia 6 years after surgery. CONCLUSION: Postoperative achalasia is a rare complication of lung surgery. Although the causal mechanism in this case could not be established, perioperative vagal nerve or esophageal plexus injury was considered a possible mechanism. Careful handling of the vagus nerve and cautious use of energy devices near the esophagus may help prevent this complication, and achalasia should be considered in patients with persistent dysphagia after lung surgery.

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未给细胞系、对照设置、样本量、具体统计值及体内数据；“显著”无P值/CI支持；结论从体外细胞与3D球模型外推到NSCLC治疗需谨慎。

papers.reason: 为NSCLC铁死亡纳米联合治疗提供体外机制与递送可行性基线，但对当前手术患者选择、随访决策或结节风险判断无直接影响。
papers.abstract_en: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a lethal malignant tumor worldwide. Although ferroptosis offers a promising route for curcumin-mediated non-small-cell lung cancer therapy, its efficacy is often constrained by the robust antioxidant defense maintained by the SLC7A11/GSH/GPX4 axis, which continuously sustains cystine uptake, glutathione biosynthesis, and GPX4-dependent lipid peroxide detoxification, thereby maintaining cellular homeostasis. Herein, we developed a glutathione-responsive metal-organic framework nanoplatform for the co-delivery of curcumin and a GPX4-targeting antisense oligonucleotide (ASO). After cellular internalization, the disulfide-bearing framework underwent GSH-triggered disassembly, enabling synchronized release of curcumin and ASO while depleting the intracellular GSH. Released curcumin increased ROS accumulation and disturbed redox homeostasis, whereas ASO silenced GPX4 expression to concurrently disable the antioxidant defense. Flow cytometry and Western blot assays confirmed significant ROS accumulation and SLC7A11 downregulation, which were detailed by molecular dynamics simulations with putative binding modes. Furthermore, the nanocomposite demonstrated robust anticancer effects in 3D multicellular tumor spheroids with a promoted oxidative imbalance. Taken together, this coordinated intervention disrupted the SLC7A11/GSH/GPX4 antioxidant axis, amplified lipid peroxidation, impaired mitochondrial function, and ultimately enhanced ferroptotic vulnerability.

papers.abstract_en: Epidemiological and occupational studies increasingly link respirable particulate matter (PM), including mineral dust, exposure with elevated lung cancer risk, yet the immunological mechanisms underlying these associations remain poorly defined. In this study, we investigated how compositionally distinct respirable PMs affect natural killer (NK) cells, a key component of immune surveillance. Using in vitro exposure and K562 target-cell challenge models, we show that respirable mineral-containing PMs induce dose- and composition-dependent NK-cell injury, including increased apoptosis/necrosis, altered cytokine profiles, changes in perforin/granzyme B-associated functions, and impaired effector responses under tumor-cell challenge conditions. Silica- and silicate-rich particles caused the most pronounced dysfunction, whereas iron-bearing and carbonaceous dusts produced distinct patterns of oxidative injury and cell loss. Mechanistic analyses identified mitochondrial depolarization, reduced mitochondrial mass, and lysosomal deacidification as convergent organelle stress pathways associated with altered NK-cell function. Ascorbic acid-associated improvements in organelle function and IFN-γ production further support a contribution of ROS-associated organelle dysfunction to impaired NK-cell responses. Collectively, these findings provide the first integrated adverse outcome pathways linking respirable PM exposure to NK-cell dysfunction, highlighting oxidative stress-driven lysosomal and mitochondrial injury as central pathways that may compromise NK-cell-mediated immune surveillance under tumor-cell challenge conditions.

papers.authors: Zhang L, Wu Y, Su P, Wang M, Shi P
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, The Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University and Hebei Tumor Hosp…
papers.results: 两例估计出血量均<150 mL；最终病理均为结节性甲状腺肿。Case 1术中发生局灶性喉返神经离断并即时行端端吻合，术后3个月喉镜示右侧声带活动受限，但无明显声嘶、主观发声不满、呛咳或临床误吸。Case 2术后3个月喉镜无显著异常，无发声/吞咽不适。两例短期随访均无呼吸窘迫、临床显著钙/PTH异常、症状性低钙血症或临床复发。
papers.authors_conclusion: 两例提示隆突水平巨大胸骨后甲状腺肿需个体化选择手术入路；当病灶与颈段甲状腺及纵隔部分连续、且纵隔部分、下极血管、喉返神经与甲状旁腺可在直视下安全控制时，选择性病例采用颈前入路是合理的；当颈部暴露不足时，尤其对纵隔部分深在且颈段体积小的老年患者，T形延长颈前切口是有效辅助；重视喉返神经处理、甲状旁腺血供保护及术中灵活调整暴露，是实现完整切除与低并发症的关键。
papers.ai_note: 仅2例、无对照，属最低级别证据，无法支撑'低并发症'的量化结论；结论中'低并发症'与Case 1喉返神经离断的事实存在口径张力。'选择性T形延长'的指征系术后归纳，存在事后叙述与选择性报告偏倚；两例为非同质对照（颈段体积、隆突下延伸深度不同），术式差异与结局差异不能互为因果。随访仅3个月，'无临床复发'对良性结节性甲状腺肿意义有限且证据力弱；嗓音/吞咽结局仅用描述性喉镜与主观询问，无客观量表或声学检查；摘要未报告手术时间、住院日、引流与血肿等围术期指标，也缺乏失血量具体测定方式。

pico.p: 2例女性，年龄74岁与81岁，2025年因巨大胸骨后甲状腺肿（一例累及隆突，一例延伸至隆突下约1 cm）接受手术
pico.ic: 颈前入路手术切除：Case 1为单纯颈前切口；Case 2在颈前切口基础上加做T形延长切口以改善暴露；无对照组

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Giant retrosternal goiter may extend to the carina or below while remaining biologically benign. The main operative challenge is not size alone but whether the mediastinal component can be safely mobilized under direct control of the airway, inferior vessels, recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN), and parathyroid blood supply. We report two elderly patients with carina-level giant retrosternal goiters to illustrate individualized surgical route selection between a cervical incision alone and a cervical incision with selective T-shaped extended. CASE PRESENTATION: Two women aged 74 and 81 years underwent surgery for giant retrosternal goiter in 2025. Both underwent contrast-enhanced CT of the neck and chest, thyroid function testing, anesthetic assessment, multidisciplinary operative planning with thoracic surgical support, and preoperative blood typing and cross-matching with blood products available according to institutional protocol. In Case 1, the goiter had a substantial cervical component and extended to the carina. Complete resection was achieved through a cervical incision, but focal RLN transection occurred during difficult inferior-pole/thoracic-inlet dissection and was repaired immediately by end-to-end anastomosis. In Case 2, most of the goiter was retrosternal with minimal cervical bulk and extended approximately 1 cm below the carina. T-shaped extended cervical incision was added to improve exposure, allowing controlled complete resection with RLN preservation. Estimated blood loss was less than 150 mL in both patients. Final pathology confirmed nodular goiter. At 3 months, Case 1 had impaired right vocal-fold movement on laryngoscopy but no obvious hoarseness, subjective voice dissatisfaction, choking, or clinical aspiration. Case 2 had no significant laryngoscopic abnormality or voice/swallowing complaint. Both patients had no respiratory compromise, clinically significant calcium/PTH abnormality, symptomatic hypocalcemia, or clinical recurrence during short-term follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: These two cases illustrate the need for individualized surgical route selection in carina-level giant retrosternal goiter. A cervical approach may be reasonable in selected patients when the lesion remains continuous with the cervical thyroid and the mediastinal component, inferior vessels, RLN, and parathyroid glands can be controlled safely under direct visualization. A T-shaped extended cervical incision is an effective adjunct when cervical exposure is inadequate, especially in elderly patients with a deep mediastinal component and minimal cervical bulk. Careful management of the recurrent laryngeal nerve, protection of the parathyroid blood supply, and intraoperative willingness to customize the exposure are essential for achieving complete resection with low morbidity.

papers.abstract_en: Immunochemotherapy (ICT) is a critical treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), yet predicting individual response remains challenging. We developed a three-channel 3D deep learning framework integrating tumor habitat analysis for predicting ICT response. In this multicenter retrospective study of 277 patients, voxel-level clustering of pretreatment CT images segmented tumors into habitat subregions reflecting microenvironmental heterogeneity. A ResNet-50 model incorporating habitat maps, cropped tumor images, and ROI masks achieved an AUC of 0.927 (95% CI, 0.850-0.951) in the independent external test cohort, compared with 0.869 for habitat radiomics (DeLong p = 0.343). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified texture features, particularly gray-level co-occurrence matrix correlation in habitat 3, as the primary contributors. This framework provides a noninvasive approach for predicting ICT response in LA-ESCC.

papers.authors: Ruan Y, Xue H, Long C, Cao W, Han J, Zhang T
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First People's Hospital of Jiande, Jiande, China.
papers.results: TP53突变与更短PFS/rwPFS相关（HR 1.65, 95%CI 1.15-2.37），并与更差OS/rwOS相关（HR 1.55, 95%CI 1.14-2.12）；EGFR L858R对比19外显子缺失与更短PFS/rwPFS相关（HR 1.62, 95%CI 1.39-1.90）及更差OS/rwOS（HR 1.63, 95%CI 1.40-1.88），敏感性分析结果一致；ECOG PS≥2、中枢神经系统/脑转移、肝转移与更差结局相关；肝转移与OS/rwOS的关联对替代效应量选择敏感；骨转移与PD-L1表达的证据稳健性较差。
papers.authors_conclusion: 证据分级评定将EGFR L858R、ECOG PS≥2和中枢神经系统/脑转移列为高确定性不良预后因素；肝转移对PFS/rwPFS为中等确定性，对OS/rwOS确定性较低；TP53突变、PD-L1表达和骨转移为较低确定性或探索性发现。这些结果支持未来构建整合预后模型，但不足以确立在一线奥希替尼单药之上选择强化治疗的标准。
papers.ai_note: 检索截止日期写作2026年5月20日，晚于常规可核实时点，需核对；摘要仅给出TP53与L858R的合并HR，ECOG PS≥2、脑转移、肝转移、骨转移、PD-L1均无任何数值，却据此作出“高/中/低确定性”分级，分级依据（GRADE域、偏倚风险、异质性I²、发表偏倚）未报告；纳入研究多为真实世界回顾性队列，混杂调整不一致，预后因素合并结果易受未调整混杂影响；“高确定性”表述与二手数据证据强度不相称；主要终点PFS/rwPFS与OS/rwOS混并（临床研究PFS与真实世界rwPFS合并），削弱可解释性。

pico.p: 18项研究、4,070例接受一线奥希替尼治疗的EGFR突变晚期/复发/转移性NSCLC患者
pico.ic: 暴露/预后因素（TP53突变、EGFR L858R对比19外显子缺失、ECOG PS≥2、中枢神经系统/脑转移、肝转移、骨转移、PD-L1表达）与结局（PFS/rwPFS为主要结局，OS/rwOS为次要结局）的关联；无干预对照

papers.reason: 为EGFR突变晚期NSCLC一线奥希替尼的患者风险分层提供合并效应量基线，可用于预后模型构建与强化治疗试验的富集人群设计（如TP53突变、L858R、脑转移亚组），但不足以单独改变一线用药选择。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is the standard first-line therapy for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but outcomes remain heterogeneous. This meta-analysis evaluated baseline clinical and molecular prognostic factors associated with poorer outcomes in this setting. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 20 May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with EGFR-mutated advanced, recurrent, or metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line osimertinib with extractable prognostic data. The primary outcome was progression-free survival or real-world progression-free survival (PFS/rwPFS); overall survival or real-world overall survival (OS/rwOS) was secondary. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models. RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 4,070 first-line osimertinib-treated patients were included. TP53 mutation was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-2.37) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.14-2.12). EGFR L858R, versus exon 19 deletion, was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39-1.90) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.40-1.88), with consistent estimates across sensitivity analyses. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status ≥ 2, central nervous system/brain metastasis, and liver metastasis were associated with poorer outcomes. The OS/rwOS association for liver metastasis was sensitive to alternative estimate selection. Evidence for bone metastasis and programmed death-ligand 1 expression was less robust. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence-tier assessment identified EGFR L858R, ECOG PS ≥ 2, and CNS/brain metastasis as high-certainty adverse prognostic factors. Liver metastasis was supported by moderate certainty for PFS/rwPFS but lower certainty for OS/rwOS. TP53 mutation, PD-L1 expression, and bone metastasis were lower-certainty or exploratory findings. These findings support future integrated prognostic models, but do not establish criteria for selecting intensified first-line therapy over osimertinib monotherapy.

papers.authors: Sakiyama K, Serapio A, Ye M, Nowroozi A, Bondarenko M, Wu YF, Qi K, Liu J et al.
papers.authors_conclusion: 规划器-执行器式多模态智能体系统能可靠回答LCS相关的患者个体化问题；其较高的工具调用与自我调节表现显示其有潜力成为LCS项目中安全有效的数字化沟通辅助工具。
papers.ai_note: ①问题为模拟生成而非真实患者提问，未验证真实语境下的提问分布与误解模式；②“自我调节准确率”以LLM-as-a-judge判定，缺少医师金标准对照，属循环式评价风险；③工具调用分母694与699题不一致，5题缺失原因未说明；④“100条回答×4名医师”与结果中228/172的分母关系需读者自行推断，报告口径不清；⑤仅报告“全 reader 满分5.0”这一严苛但粗糙的比例，未给均值/分布或失败案例的错误类型分析；⑥无与基线模型、检索式问答或人工护士/医师回答的对照；⑦单中心回顾性数据，无真实随访依从性等临床结局。

pico.p: 某三级学术医院116份肺癌筛查（LCS）CT报告及图像；基于此生成699个模拟患者问题（分为可回答与应转诊医生两类）；医师阅片评分子集为4名医师×100条回答
pico.ic: 干预：基于大语言模型的多智能体（planner+executor）多模态智能体系统，用于回答LCS CT结果相关问题；对照：无对照组，仅以工具调用准确率、自我调节准确率（LLM-as-a-judge）及医师评分（临床准确性、患者可理解性）为评价指标

papers.reason: 为肺癌筛查结果沟通类AI工具提供了可复用的评价框架（工具调用、越界问题转诊、医师多维评分），可作为后续真实患者场景研究与数字沟通工具对照设计的基线；但尚不足以改变当前筛查随访或患者沟通的临床路径。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurate patient understanding of lung cancer screening (LCS) results is critical for engagement and follow-up adherence, given the currently low screening uptake. While artificial intelligence (AI) systems show promise in facilitating patient communication, its effective use in clinical settings requires appropriate invocation of imaging tools and self-regulation by deferring certain questions to physicians. To this end, we developed and evaluated a planner-executor style multimodal agentic system to answer simulated patient questions about LCS CT results. METHODS: This retrospective study utilized 116 LCS CT reports and images collected from a tertiary academic hospital. The system employed a multi-agent architecture (planner and executor) to mimic clinical reasoning. We developed a large language model (LLM)-based question generation framework to prepare a comprehensive set of 699 simulated patient questions, categorized as answerable and defer-to-doctor to assess self-regulation. Performance was evaluated on tool-calling, self-regulation accuracy (ability to correctly defer out-of-scope questions to a human provider) assessed by LLM-as-a-judge, and clinical quality assessed by a reader performance study with four physicians evaluating a subset of 100 responses. RESULTS: The system demonstrated high overall tool-calling accuracy of 93.1% (646/694; 95% CI: 91.2%, 95.0%) and self-regulation accuracy of 92.6% (462/499; 90.2%, 94.8%). For answerable questions, the percentage of responses receiving perfect 5.0 scores across all readers included 78.9% (180/228) for clinical accuracy (inter-rater agreement: Gwet's AC2=0.92), and 73.2% (167/228) for patient understandability (0.86). For defer-to-doctor questions, the percentage of responses included 77.3% (133/172) for clinical accuracy (0.80) and 70.3% (121/172) for patient understandability (0.78). CONCLUSIONS: The planner-executor style multi-modal agentic system reliably answers patient-specific questions about LCS. Its high tool-calling and self-regulation performance demonstrates its potential as a safe and effective digital communication facilitator in LCS programs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component. METHOD: Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded. RESULTS: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology. CONCLUSIONS: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for lung cancer or other pulmonary lesions, effective one-lung ventilation (OLV) is essential to provide surgical exposure. Bronchial blockers (BBs) are increasingly used for OLV, but the optimal management of their vent port to accelerate lung collapse remains unclear. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, controlled trial, 75 patients were allocated to three groups (n = 25 each): Group 1-BB with vent port closed; Group 2 (control)-BB with vent port open; Group 3-BB with the disconnection technique. Primary outcome was the time to complete lung collapse, which was scored according to the video clips obtained during the operation. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hypoxemia, blood gas analysis, blocker malposition, perioperative complications, and surgeon satisfaction. RESULTS: A total of 72 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, with 24 patients in each group. Median time to complete lung collapse was 15 min (95% CI: 10-15) in Groups 1 and 3 but was not reached in Group 2 (15/24, 62.5% had not achieved complete collapse by 30 min). In an exploratory 30-min restricted mean survival time (RMST), complete collapse occurred on average 14.17 min earlier in Group 1 (95% CI: 11.10-17.23) and 12.50 min earlier in Group 3 (95% CI: 9.62-15.38) than in Group 2, with no difference between Groups 1 and 3 (1.67 min, 95% CI: -1.85 to 5.19); time-averaged hazard ratios were consistent (Group 1 vs. 2, 9.80 [4.22-22.73]; Group 3 vs. 2, 7.63 [3.36-17.31]; Group 1 vs. 3, 1.20 [0.67-2.16]). No significant differences were detected in hypoxemia, blocker malposition, or complications across groups; however, the trial was not powered for safety outcomes. CONCLUSION: In patients aged 18-65 years with ASA I-II and normal pulmonary function undergoing thoracic surgery, the closure of the BB vent port results in a more rapid lung collapse compared to maintaining the vent port open. However, there was no statistically significant difference observed between the vent port closure technique and the disconnection technique regarding the time required for complete lung collapse. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR identifier: ChiCTR2000039896.

papers.title_en: Nodal evaluation as the arbiter of oncologic equivalence: reassessing segmentectomy after CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802.
papers.authors: Bazarbaev A, Androutsopoulou V, Zotos PA, Abbaker N, Scarci M, Magouliotis DE
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Surgery, Duke University Medical Center, Durham, NC, United States.

papers.abstract_en: Two randomized trials, CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802, established segmentectomy as an oncologically acceptable alternative to lobectomy for small, peripheral, clinically node-negative non-small cell lung cancer. Both reached that conclusion under a protocol-enforced condition that is rarely emphasized when their results are applied in practice: nodal status had to be verified intraoperatively against a defined anatomic standard. CALGB 140503 required frozen-section confirmation of N0 status at two mediastinal stations and one major hilar node before randomization, whereas JCOG0802 mandated systematic or selective dissection of N1 and N2 stations in both arms and explicitly disallowed sampling as a substitute. This review examines whether that nodal rigor is reproduced, or even reported, once segmentectomy leaves the trial setting. National data indicate that it is not. Segmentectomy accounts for 4.4% of resections for clinical stage I to IIA disease, and only 12.6% of segmentectomy cases met all three Commission on Cancer quality measures, with adherence concentrated in academic and higher-volume programs. Retrospective series consistently report lower nodal upstaging after segmentectomy than after lobectomy, but the difference is driven by N1 rather than N2 stations and tracks the smaller nodal footprint of the operation, so a lower upstaging rate cannot by itself distinguish less disease from less looking. Anatomic mapping data indicate that exhaustive intersegmental dissection is unnecessary, whereas reliable hilar and mediastinal sampling is not. Across the wider literature, adequate nodal evaluation is defined inconsistently and reported at a granularity too coarse for readers to verify compliance, a two-axis problem that we characterize here for the segmentectomy literature specifically. Robotic assistance increases the number of nodal stations harvested relative to video-assisted surgery but has not been shown to improve risk-adjusted detection of occult disease. We propose a seven-point minimum standard, anchored on station-based rather than count-based adequacy, for segmentectomy performed outside a clinical trial.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) features a poor prognosis and unclear pathogenesis, and the role of R-loops, key regulators of genome stability, has not been systematically characterized in this disease. METHODS: Transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data of ESCC were integrated with published R-loop-related genes (RLRGs) to construct an RLRG scoring system. The associations between the RLRG score and prognosis, tumor immune microenvironment, and tumor stemness were analyzed via multiple bioinformatics algorithms. The expression of core genes was verified using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western Blot, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: Seven key RLRGs related to the prognosis of the ESCC patients were identified, among which three core genes-BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155-were significantly upregulated in ESCC tissues compared with controls, as confirmed by both bioinformatic analysis and experimental validation. Notably, BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155 were co-enriched in DNA replication, pyrimidine metabolism, RNA degradation, and MYC target pathways, which are closely linked to R-loop biology and suggest potential crosstalk between these genes and R-loop regulatory networks. Meanwhile, the low RLRGs score group exhibited significantly worse overall survival but displayed a more active yet dysfunctional immune microenvironment. Single-cell analysis identified SquamousEpithelium cells as the key cell type with the highest RLRG scores across five independent algorithms. Malignant SquamousEpithelium cells with high RLRG scores showed enhanced stemness and activation of pathways including JAK-STAT, hypoxia, and DNA repair. CONCLUSION: This study provided the first systematic characterization of the R-loop landscape in ESCC, suggests that SquamousEpithelium cells may play a key role in R-loop-associated progression and are identified as potential prognostic biomarkers with possible therapeutic relevance that requires functional validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking is the primary cause of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in Norway. To inform disease modeling and tobacco control policies, including lung cancer screening, we estimated sex-specific, birth-cohort smoking behaviors among Norwegians born between 1950 and 2000 using national survey data. METHODS: We analyzed nationally representative cross-sectional survey data from 1978 to 2024 (n = 78,282) to reconstruct smoking trends and smoking intensity in Norway. We used a previously established Age-Period-Cohort modeling framework to estimate cohort-specific prevalence of daily ever-smoking, probabilities of smoking initiation and cessation, prevalence of daily current-smoking, and average cigarettes smoked per day (CPD). Analyses were conducted separately by sex assigned at birth for cohorts born between 1950 and 2000. FINDINGS: Daily ever-smoking prevalence peaked in the 1950 birth cohort, reaching 70% (90% CI 66%-91%) among males and 66% (90% CI 55%-89%) among females, alongside similar peaks in smoking initiation probabilities, 13% (90% CI 12%-24%) for males and 12% (90% CI 10%-23%) for females. Smoking cessation probabilities increased with age within each birth cohort, rising from approximately 0% to 5% over 40 years in earlier cohorts, compared with an increase from about 5% to 15% over 20 years from the 1965 birth cohort onward. Smoking intensity peaked at 15 CPD among males and 12 CPD among females. Although smoking intensity declined in both sexes after the 1975 birth cohort, it remained higher among males, with peak model-estimated CPD decreasing from approximately 13.5 to 10 cigarettes in males and from 11.5 to 7.5 cigarettes in females between the 1980 and 2000 birth cohorts. INTERPRETATION: Smoking behavior in Norway has changed across generations, with declining smoking initiation rates, increased smoking cessation, and lower cigarettes per day. Understanding these trends provides essential inputs to inform tobacco control and lung cancer prevention policies in Norway. FUNDING: Norwegian Cancer Society, National Cancer Institute of the National Institutes of Health, U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

papers.abstract_en: IntroductionZenocutuzumab-zbco is the first approved therapy for NRG1 fusion-positive cancer, indicated for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA). At the pivotal analyses, overall survival (OS) was unreported for NSCLC and PDAC, whereas a later publication reported observed OS and progression-free survival (PFS) for CCA. Cost-effectiveness was evaluated from a US payer perspective.MethodsA three-state partitioned survival model estimated incremental costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) over 5 years. For NSCLC and PDAC, OS was modeled as a threshold variable across prespecified scenarios, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per scenario. For CCA, OS and PFS were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves and used directly, with a base-case ICER and extrapolation sensitivity. The wholesale acquisition cost was $24,155.46/infusion. Probabilistic, one-way, and threshold analyses were performed.ResultsFor NSCLC and PDAC, ICERs ranged from approximately $665,000 (PDAC, OS 18 months) to $2.79 million per QALY (NSCLC, OS 10 months). For CCA, using observed data, the base-case ICER was approximately $397,000 per QALY (extrapolation range $349,000-$430,000). No indication was cost-effective at $150,000 or $200,000 per QALY. Drug acquisition cost, comparator OS, and utilities were the dominant drivers. Cost-effectiveness required acquisition-cost reductions of 60% to 91%.ConclusionsAt its current price, zenocutuzumab is not cost-effective for any approved indication, whether OS is unobserved (NSCLC, PDAC) or observed (CCA). Cost-effectiveness is achievable only through substantial price reduction. NSCLC and PDAC findings are conditional on the prespecified OS scenarios; CCA findings rest on observed survival with extrapolation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is highly heterogeneous, leading to limited drug effectiveness and resistance. Antibody therapies offer limited benefits due to low response rates. Multispecific antibodies, targeting multiple tumor antigens and natural killer (NK)-cell receptors, may overcome these challenges, but their effectiveness in ESCC therapy is not yet understood. METHODS: Transcriptome sequencing and database analysis were performed on samples from patients with ESCC to identify tumor antigens. Multispecific antibodies were designed to target tumor antigens and NK-cell surface markers. Fast protein liquid chromatography and surface plasmon resonance were applied for quality control of antibodies. Using multiple ESCC cell lines and NK cells from different donors, flow cytometry was performed to assess NK cell cytotoxicity and activation. Immunofluorescence assays were used to confirm colocalization. Transcriptome sequencing, flow cytometry and western blots were performed to explore molecular mechanisms. Subcutaneous and metastatic xenograft tumor models were established to evaluate the in vivo antitumor efficacy of antibodies combined with adoptive transfer of NK cells. RESULTS: The expression of EGFR was consistently highly expressed in all ESCC samples, while MET was specifically upregulated in recurrent ESCC, whereas the database also validated two antigens overexpression in tumor tissues. Antibodies were successfully engineered for multiple antigens binding. The tetraspecific antibodies significantly enhanced NK-cell cytotoxicity by up to 30% against ESCC and paclitaxel-resistant cell lines compared with the NK-only group in vitro. Transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation revealed that antibodies triggered immune activation pathways and increased the expression of tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, and granzyme B in NK cells, but also induced NK cell exhaustion. In vivo, tetraspecific antibodies combined with NK cell infusions exerted superior antitumor efficacy, with an 82.3% tumor volume reduction in the early-stage model and 65.7% in the advanced-stage model compared with controls. The therapeutic efficacy was also observed in the metastatic tumor model. Meanwhile, the combination therapy was well tolerated, with enhanced NK cell infiltration in tumor tissues. CONCLUSIONS: We developed tetraspecific antibodies to effectively bridge ESCC cells and NK cells. The antibodies have the potential to enhance the antitumor activity of NK cells against ESCC. This study supports the clinical translation of tetraspecific antibodies for NK cell-based immunotherapy for ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) has greatly expanded the identification of rare germline variants in hereditary cancer predisposition. However, the interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS), particularly in novel candidate genes, remains a major challenge in lung cancer genetics. OBJECTIVE: To functionally characterize selected germline variants identified by WES in patients with familial or suspected hereditary lung cancer and provide evidence for their prioritization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three splicing variants in HGS, CDK12, and CEACAM5 genes were investigated by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing to assess their effect on splicing. Candidate missense variants were analyzed through protein-protein interaction network analysis, gene expression profiling, and structure-based computational modeling to evaluate their potential impact on protein stability and molecular interactions. RESULTS: RNA analysis confirmed that the CDK12 variant produced the previously reported in-frame one amino acid deletion, whereas the HGS variant activated a cryptic splice acceptor site, resulting in an in-frame deletion affecting a region containing a known ubiquitination site. No aberrant splicing was detected for CEACAM5. Network analyses highlighted convergence of three candidate genes (ERBB3, MAP2K1 and RASA2) on receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and the RAS/MAPK pathway. Structural analyses predicted local perturbations affecting membrane interactions, residue interaction networks, or protein stability for variants in the three previous genes and in USP4, supporting their functional relevance. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating RNA-based functional assays with network and structural analyses provides a practical framework for interpreting and prioritizing rare germline VUS identified by WES, supporting the identification of candidate lung cancer susceptibility genes and improving genetic risk assessment.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Functional assays can assist individualised selection of treatment regimens by evaluating the ex vivo response of tumour cells to anticancer therapeutics. However, the two major strategies used to assess responses to targeted drugs, target-based profiling and phenotypic profiling, have inherent limitations. Target-based profiling does not directly capture downstream cell-fate outcomes, whereas phenotypic profiling provides limited mechanistic information on drug action. METHODS: Live-cell fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) microscopy was used to integrate the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 with cellular phenotypic features, thereby predicting the efficacy of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) at the single-cell level. RESULTS: The target-based drug score (T-score), derived from the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 in living cells co-expressing CFP-EGFRL858R and YFP-GRB2, enabled evaluation of the on-target activity of EGFR-TKIs against EGFRL858R. The phenotype drug score (P-score), constructed from cellular phenotype features, characterised the phenotypic responses induced by EGFR-TKIs. The TP-score, integrating the T- and P-scores, accurately predicted the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs. In living H3255 cells, the TP-score of osimertinib (OSI) was higher than that of gefitinib (GEF). Notably, in H3255 cell-derived xenograft (CDX) mouse models, OSI showed superior in vivo antitumour efficacy compared with GEF. Furthermore, live-cell TP scoring revealed that primary tumour cells from a patient with NSCLC did not respond to OSI, a finding consistent with the absence of actionable EGFR mutations in this patient. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the clinical feasibility of predicting EGFR-TKI efficacy by integrating EGFRL858R-GRB2 interactions with cellular phenotypic features in single living cells.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary resection is a primary treatment for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer, but removal of lung tissue can result in significant changes in postoperative pulmonary function and patient recovery. This review examines changes in pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and patient-reported outcomes following lung resection, with consideration of differences among surgical procedures and postoperative timepoints. Across studies, pulmonary function demonstrated its greatest decline during the early postoperative period, followed by gradual improvement during subsequent follow-up. However, pulmonary function generally remained below preoperative values, with the magnitude of decline influenced by the extent of lung tissue removed. Patients undergoing lobectomy or pneumonectomy generally experienced greater postoperative reductions than those undergoing sublobar procedures, although outcomes also varied according to the lobe and number of segments resected. Patient-reported outcomes, including dyspnea, pain, physical function, and quality of life, similarly worsened during early recovery but generally improved over time, with some measures returning to baseline. Preoperative pulmonary function, particularly DLCO, remains important for assessing a patient's ability to tolerate resection, while postoperative oxygen requirements are influenced by pulmonary function, patient characteristics, and postoperative complications. Additionally, decreased physical activity after surgery was associated with non-recovery of DLCO. Overall, postoperative pulmonary function follows a pattern of early decline followed by gradual recovery, although complete return to baseline is uncommon. These findings emphasize the importance of evaluating both pulmonary function and patient-reported outcomes when considering the consequences of pulmonary resection.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has become a biomarker-driven disease, yet durable control remains limited by therapeutic resistance, metabolic heterogeneity, and incomplete predictors of response. Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death linked to mitochondrial respiration and lipoylated TCA-cycle proteins, offers a potential metabolic layer for patient stratification. However, the current NSCLC literature is dominated by cuproptosis-related gene scores, lncRNA models, and immune-association signatures. These studies are useful for hypothesis generation but rarely demonstrate copper flux, FDX1 dependence, lipoylated DLAT/DLST engagement, iron-sulfur cluster protein loss, or pathway-specific pharmacodynamics. We therefore organize the NSCLC literature using a mechanistic evidence matrix that separates transcriptomic association, copper-access enrichment, mitochondrial-dependence evidence, canonical target engagement, and clinical pharmacodynamic confirmation. Rather than proposing a new molecular subtype or diagnostic label, we conceptualize cuproptosis susceptibility as a continuous, mechanism-based construct defined by copper access, TCA/OXPHOS dependence, lipoylated substrate burden, detoxification capacity, and immune context. This framework reframes cuproptosis from universal copper toxicity to a conditional therapeutic vulnerability. Its clinical value will depend on biomarker-enriched trials with pharmacodynamic confirmation rather than retrospective gene signatures alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Clinically important deterioration (CID) has been used to assess chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) progression by time-to-first-event analysis. However, this does not reveal the clinical importance of the CID components. The win ratio may provide a complementary assessment by comparing outcomes according to a prespecified hierarchy. We reanalysed data from the Tie-COPD studywith win ratio to assess the overall treatment benefit associated with tiotropium in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD. METHODS: In this exploratory post hoc study, the unmatched win ratio method was applied to the outcomes observed in the Tie-COPD study comparing 18 µg tiotropium with placebo in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD over 24 months. CID was defined as an occurrence of moderate-to-severe exacerbation, an increase of ≥2 units in COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score or a decrease of ≥100 mL in the forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1). We evaluated the win ratio across all possible hierarchies of CID components. Exploratory inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW), and covariate-adjusted IPCW (CovIPCW) analyses were performed to account for censoring. Subgroup analyses were performed with stratification by sex, smoking status, Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease stage, CAT score and modified Medical Research Council score at baseline. RESULTS: Of the 841 randomised patients, 771 were included in the full analysis set (tiotropium=388; placebo=383). With the clinical hierarchy of CID defined by FEV1, exacerbation and CAT, the win ratio was 2.26 (95% CI 1.87 to 2.73, p<0.001), and the net benefit was 0.35 (95% CI 0.27 to 0.44, p<0.001). Win ratios were greater than 1 across all hierarchies, subgroups and censoring-adjusted analyses. No treatment-by-subgroup interaction was detected (all p for interaction >0.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post hoc analysis, tiotropium was associated with a greater overall treatment benefit than placebo in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD. This benefit was also observed in patients with mild disease or fewer respiratory symptoms. The direction of the findings was consistent across alternative CID hierarchies and censoring-adjusted analyses. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT01455129.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and prognosis in patients with oesophageal cancer undergoing radiotherapy, and to evaluate the incremental prognostic value of combining SII with clinical TNM stage. METHOD: A retrospective analysis was performed on 159 patients with locally advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma who received radiotherapy. The optimal cut-off value for pre-radiotherapy SII was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and patients were stratified into low- and high-SII groups accordingly. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were employed to identify independent prognostic factors. The predictive performance of SII alone, TNM stage alone, and their combination was compared. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). RESULTS: The optimal pre-radiotherapy SII cut-off was 506.63. SII showed a tendency to increase during the course of radiotherapy. Short-term efficacy in the low-SII group was significantly better than that in the high-SII group (p = 0.042). Significant differences were observed between the two groups in 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year OS and PFS rates (all p < 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified tumour location, TNM stage, gross tumour volume, and pre-radiotherapy SII as independent prognostic factors (all p < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of SII and TNM stage in predicting survival was significantly larger than that of SII or TNM stage alone. The combined SII-TNM model demonstrated superior predictive performance compared with either parameter individually (both p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Pre-radiotherapy SII serves as an independent prognostic factor in oesophageal cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy, with higher SII values associated with poorer survival outcomes. Integrating SII with TNM stage provides enhanced predictive accuracy for prognosis in this patient population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) shows marked heterogeneity in its immune microenvironment, which may contribute to differences in disease-free survival (DFS) and clinical outcome. Although current LUAD classifications are largely based on genomic or transcriptomic features, immune subtypes defined directly from bulk proteomic data remain poorly characterized. Here, we used an immune-cell proteomic reference matrix to investigate proteome-defined immune states in LUAD and to identify prognostically relevant immune subtypes. METHODS: A quantitative human immune-cell proteomic reference matrix was integrated with LUAD tumor proteomic profiles. The reference matrix covered seven major immune lineages and 26 immune-cell states. The discovery cohort included 101 LUAD tumor proteomes with matched clinical information. After gene symbol matching and normalization, proteome-defined immune-cell state signals were estimated for each sample using non-negative constrained regression. These signals were then used for unsupervised subtype identification and DFS analysis. An independent Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)-LUAD cohort was used for validation, with subtype analysis performed at the immune-cell marker protein module level. RESULTS: The immune-cell reference matrix contained 8400 quantified proteins, and 2381 proteins were retained for modeling. Based on 26 proteome-defined immune-cell state signals, LUAD samples separated into two immune proteomic subtypes. In the discovery cohort, Subtype 2 had significantly worse DFS than Subtype 1 (log-rank p = 0.0047; HR = 2.09, 95% CI 1.24-3.54). In the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)-LUAD validation cohort, marker protein module-based analysis again identified two subtypes with distinct DFS outcomes. The high-risk Subtype 2 showed higher Granulocyte and Myeloid/DC modules, whereas the low-risk Subtype 1 showed higher B cell, T cell, and NK-cell modules. Subtype 2 was associated with shorter DFS in the validation cohort (log-rank p = 0.0061; HR = 3.45, 95% CI: 1.35-8.82), and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, and stage. CONCLUSIONS: Proteomic immune profiling identified two prognostically distinct immune subtypes in LUAD. papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer screening (LCS) remains underutilized, with 18% uptake nationally, despite established evidence-based guidelines, particularly among women who engage with preventive care through breast cancer screening (BCS). We characterized baseline LCS uptake and its correlates among women receiving BCS at two participating hospitals. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using six years of electronic health record data (October 2019-November 2025) from Barnes-Jewish West County Hospital and Christian Hospital. We conducted multivariable logistic regression models and assessed for effect modification by race and area deprivation using likelihood ratio tests. Results Of 9,686 women with smoking history, 3,209 (33.1%) had received at least one LCS. Pack-year documentation status (AOR 2.90; 95% CI: 2.63, 3.19), tobacco cessation medication use (AOR 2.21; 95% CI: 1.98, 2.48), and current smoking (AOR 1.84; 95% CI: 1.64, 2.07) were the factors most strongly associated with uptake. Non-Hispanic Black women had lower adjusted odds of obtaining LCS compared to non-Hispanic White women (AOR 0.87; 95% CI: 0.78, 0.98); estimates in the smaller pack-year subgroups were similar in direction but imprecise. Alcohol use was associated with lower odds of LCS uptake (0.81, 95% CI: 0.73, 0.89). Effect modification by race and area deprivation were not significant. Conclusions Baseline LCS uptake exceeded the national average; however, racial disparities were observed. Completeness of smoking history documentation, tobacco cessation medication use, and current smoking status were strongly associated with LCS uptake. These findings highlight the need for strategies to improve smoking history documentation and promote tobacco cessation efforts in cancer screening programs and establish the baseline against which the Pink & Pearl program, a co-located breast and lung cancer screening initiative at these sites, will be evaluated.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The 8th American Joint Committee on Cancer postneoadjuvant pathologic stage grouping is the current standard for risk stratification after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy. However, its prognostic ordering may be unstable in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, particularly across intermediate stage groups. METHODS: Patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by esophagectomy at two centers were retrospectively identified. The West China Hospital cohort was used for development, and the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University cohort was used for external validation. Recursive partitioning analysis using routine ypT and ypN categories was applied to develop a revised stage grouping. Prognostic ordering, model fit, and discrimination were compared with the 8th American Joint Committee on Cancer postneoadjuvant stage grouping. RESULTS: Among 1486 patients, 872 were included in the development cohort and 614 in the validation cohort. The revised system grouped patients into 5 prognostic categories and restored an ordered survival gradient in both cohorts, whereas the current American Joint Committee on Cancer stage showed survival overlap and inversion between stages II and IIIA. The revised system showed higher linear trend chi-square and likelihood ratio chi-square values and lower Akaike information criterion values in both cohorts. Concordance index and time-dependent area under the curve values were comparable between the two systems. CONCLUSIONS: The revised ypT/ypN-based stage grouping improved prognostic ordering and model fit in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, while maintaining comparable discrimination. This approach may support postoperative risk stratification after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Renal injury is an adverse effect of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) inhibitor therapy. We investigated factors associated with renal injury and renal outcomes by VEGF inhibitor type in lung cancer. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 441 lung cancer patients treated with VEGF inhibitors. The primary cohort comprised 376 patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2, negative dipstick proteinuria, and no hematuria at baseline; 65 patients underwent exploratory analysis. The primary composite renal outcome was incident proteinuria and/or eGFR decline >20% from baseline within 1 year. Cox models adjusted for clinical, tumor, and treatment covariates. Landmark and overlap-weighted sensitivity analyses were performed. Proteinuria and eGFR decline were analyzed separately. RESULTS: The primary composite renal outcome occurred in 250 patients (66.5%); among patients with an event, the median time to first event was 92.0 days. Diabetes mellitus (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.17-3.05), higher body mass index (BMI) (aHR per 1-kg/m2 increase, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.09), and lower hemoglobin (aHR per 10-g/L increase, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.79-0.94) were independently associated with the primary outcome. VEGF inhibitor type was not associated with the primary outcome (overall p = 0.690), with similar overlap-weighted results. Incident proteinuria occurred in 120 patients (31.9%) and was associated with diabetes and lower hemoglobin; eGFR decline >20% occurred in 188 patients (50.0%) and was associated with lower hemoglobin. Platinum-containing chemotherapy showed a time-varying association with incident proteinuria. CONCLUSION: The primary composite renal outcome was common during the first year of VEGF inhibitor therapy. In the primary cohort, diabetes mellitus, higher BMI, and lower baseline hemoglobin were associated with this outcome, whereas no statistically significant association was observed for VEGF inhibitor type. These findings warrant validation in independent cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: In advanced stages, lung adenocarcinoma obstructs airways and disrupts ventilation-perfusion relationships in the lung, causing systemic hypoxemia and enabling a feed-forward loop that accelerates malignancy. Systemic hypoxemia is also experienced due to common respiratory comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), potentially accelerating malignancy. In a statewide electronic health record network, pre-existing COPD (598 matched pairs) or sleep apnea (235 matched pairs) independently predicted worse survival following incident lung cancer diagnosis. Since the mechanistic basis of the link between malignancy and hypoxia is not well understood, we created systemic hypoxia in Kras LSL- G12D/+ ;Trp53 fl/fl (KP) mice by delivering low inspired oxygen concentrations (8% inspired oxygen; 8 h daily). Hypoxia nearly doubled tumor multiplicity and selectively remodeled cancer central carbon metabolism. Spatially resolved metabolomics revealed marked tumor-compartment glycogen accumulation, elevated tricarboxylic-acid cycle intermediates, and depleted glycolytic pools. Quantitative proteomics across cellular models and autochthonous tumors demonstrated that systemic hypoxia drives glycogen mobilization selectively through the lysosomal enzyme acid α-glucosidase (GAA). Tumor-cell-autonomous deletion of GAA eliminated the hypoxia-driven growth advantage and disrupted downstream anabolic biosynthetic pathways. Thus, systemic hypoxia drives lung adenocarcinoma expansion by mobilizing lysosomal glycogen reserves through GAA to sustain proliferative growth. HIGHLIGHTS: Systemic hypoxia acts as an intrinsic driver of lung adenocarcinoma progression.Controlled systemic hypoxia doubles tumor multiplicity and reprograms cancer metabolism.Hypoxic tumors mobilize glycogen via lysosomal GAA independently of HIF-1α stabilization.Tumor-cell-autonomous deletion of GAA eliminates the hypoxia-mediated growth advantage in vivo.Pre-existing COPD and sleep apnea exacerbate hypoxemic burden and worsen clinical survival. ETOC BLURB: Lung tumors compromise pulmonary gas exchange, driving systemic hypoxemia that accelerates malignancy. Comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obstructive sleep apnea compound this hypoxemic burden. Clarke et al. isolate systemic hypoxia in mice, showing it doubles lung tumor multiplicity by inducing glycogen degradation through lysosomal acid α-glucosidase (GAA). Deleting GAA eliminates this hypoxic growth advantage.

papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to describe trends in survival by treatment modality in advanced-stage (III-IV) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. A retrospective observational study was conducted. Patients diagnosed with primary NSCLC stage III-IV were included from the Cancer Registry of the Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi, Pakistan. A flexible parametric (Royston-Parmar) model was used to estimate survival trends by treatment modality, sex, and age group. Overall, 663 patients were included; 489 (73.76%) were males. Eighty-one (12.22%) received 'radiotherapy only', 217 (32.73%) 'systemic therapy only', 136 (20.51%) 'systemic therapy with radiotherapy', 34 (5.13%) underwent 'surgery ± additional treatment', and 195 (29.41%) did not receive any treatment. Overall, predicted survival increased across all treatment modalities from 2011 to 2019, including the 'no treatment' group. In stage III disease, the absolute change in 1- and 2-year survival was most pronounced in the 'radiotherapy only' group, at 25.71% and 20.62%, respectively. In stage IV disease, the absolute change in 1-year survival was largest in the 'no treatment' group (24.44%) and in 2-year survival in the 'surgery ± additional treatment' group (33.46%). For 'surgery ± additional treatment' in stage III disease, patients aged >60 years had significantly lower odds of receiving surgery [odds ratio (OR) 0.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.09-0.70, p=0.008]. Among stage IV patients, those diagnosed in 2017-2019 had significantly lower odds of receiving 'radiotherapy only' (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.23-0.92, p=0.027), while squamous cell carcinoma histology was associated with significantly higher odds of receiving 'radiotherapy only' (OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.06-4.71, p=0.036). In conclusion, survival improved across all treatment modalities, including among untreated patients. Survival differences across modalities, including with surgical resection and combined therapy, most likely reflect selection of patients with more favorable prognostic profiles. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as real-world treatment patterns and associated survival trends rather than evidence of comparative treatment efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) mediastinal mass excision has become the standard approach for anterior mediastinal lesions. Understanding its learning curve is essential for surgical training and quality assurance. The primary objective was to quantify the association between cumulative case experience (case sequence number) and operative time, the primary outcome, using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis and multivariable regression modelling. We tested the null hypothesis that operative time does not change with increasing case sequence after adjustment for patient-, tumour- and country-related factors. Secondary objectives were to estimate the number of cases required to achieve proficiency and to compare perioperative outcomes across learning phases and between participating countries. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at five academic and tertiary-care centers in Egypt and Saudi Arabia between January 2023 and December 2025. Seventy-seven consecutive patients undergoing VATS excision of mediastinal masses were categorized into three phases: Early (first 20 cases), Intermediate (next 20 cases), and Late (last 37 cases). Cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis was performed. Operative outcomes, including operative time, blood loss, conversion rate, and postoperative complications, were compared across phases and between countries (Egypt vs. Saudi Arabia). Multivariable linear regression and a linear mixed-effects model with participating centre as a random intercept were used to identify factors independently associated with operative time. RESULTS: Mean operative time significantly decreased across phases (189.5 ± 21.9 vs. 156.5 ± 26.4 vs. 139.7 ± 30.5 minutes; p < 0.001). CUSUM analysis demonstrated a learning curve inflection point between cases 20 and 26. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, myasthenia gravis, presence of a discrete mass, thymic neoplasm and country, case sequence number remained independently associated with shorter operative time (β = -1.14 min per case; 95% CI -1.47 to -0.80; p < 0.001; R² = 0.48, adjusted R² = 0.42), with consistent estimates using robust standard errors and a mixed-effects model with centre as a random intercept (β = -1.37; 95% CI -1.80 to -0.95). Patients treated in Saudi Arabia (n = 7) were older and more often had discrete neoplastic masses, but operative time did not differ significantly between countries before (p = 0.128) or after adjustment (p = 0.548). Conversion to open surgery occurred in 3.9% (n = 3), all in the Intermediate and Late phases. Overall mortality was 2.6% (n = 2), both in the Late phase and associated with complex cases. No significant differences were observed regarding ICU stay, hospital stay, or postoperative complications. CONCLUSION: VATS mediastinal mass excision is safe and feasible, with surgical proficiency achieved after approximately 20-26 cases. Operative time was the most reliable indicator of learning progression, and the learning effect persisted after multivariable adjustment for patient-, tumour- and country-related factors. Structured mentorship and careful case selection are recommended during the early learning phase.

papers.abstract_en: Background The management of suspected malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is often variable, with many patients undergoing repeated pleural aspirations before a definitive management decision is made. The RED (respiratory rate, effusion depth and dyspnoea) score is a recently derived and validated tool that predicts the time to the next pleural fluid drainage procedure. We describe a single-center, before-and-after quality improvement project (QIP) evaluating the introduction of a structured proforma incorporating clinical pre-test probability and the RED score into routine pleural clinic assessment. Methods A retrospective baseline cycle (Cycle 1, n=48) was compared with a prospective intervention cycle (Cycle 2, n=26) following the implementation of a structured assessment pro forma. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing unplanned emergency admission or earlier-than-planned pleural clinic review within three months of the index pleural procedure. Secondary outcomes included the proportion of patients requiring more than two pleural procedures and the proportion of patients achieving definitive pleural management within three months. Categorical variables were compared using Fisher's exact test given the small sample sizes; results are presented with risk differences, 95% confidence intervals, and odds ratios where calculable. No a priori power calculation was performed, and this exploratory before-and-after design does not permit causal inferences. Results In Cycle 1, 16/48 patients (33.3%) experienced an emergency admission or unplanned pleural clinic review, compared with 2/26 (7.7%) in Cycle 2 (Fisher's exact test, P=0.021; risk difference -25.6%, 95% CI -42.5 to -8.8; odds ratio 6.0). The proportion of patients requiring more than two pleural procedures fell from 33.3% to 22.7% (P=0.415, not statistically significant). Cytology was positive in 24/48 (50.0%) Cycle 1 patients and 10/26 (38.5%) Cycle 2 patients. The two cohorts differed descriptively in performance status (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) ≥2:41.7% vs. 87.5%, P<0.001) and malignancy type distribution. RED scores were documented only anecdotally within free-text clinical notes for a subset of Cycle 2 patients and were not systematically recorded or analyzed as a distribution. Conclusions A structured pleural assessment pathway was associated with a statistically significant reduction in emergency presentations and a non-significant reduction in repeated procedures. However, given the small, single-center, non-randomised, uncontrolled before-and-after design, differing case mix between cohorts, and incomplete RED score documentation, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating. They support further, larger, multicenter evaluations rather than immediate wider adoption.
